text:
For fairness, giving an update on @eigencloud Darkbloom.

Payout increased quite a bit after adding support for Gemma 4, following your comments and advice, as it seems to generate 10x the daily demand. Gemma  payouts are tiny, but because jobs are piling up and you can still serve the Qwen jobs, I ended up with more revenue.

This is now making a tiny profit compared to electricity costs, and as this machine was already running 24/7 doing other stuff for me, I consider it a net benefit.

100% not a real money maker, not worth spending 5k$ to buy the machine for that. 

But if you already own a machine, there's very little downside to running DarkBloom.

My overall opinion hasn't changed on the vertical, but they delivered a solid product.
author: mzeller
quoted_text:
After earning the life-changing amount of ONE DOLLAR AND TEN CENTS for around 24h of letting people use my M4 max for AI compute via @eigencloud DarkBloom product, my feedback:

1) Infra is good, seamless to setup and quite stable.
2) Very little real demand; a decent part of my revenue is just Eigen incentives
3) Model roster is bad and outdated, I think letting people use Qwen 3.8 27b would have met more success
4) I think it's as promising as "retail mining" was back then; decentralized compute is a nice idea on paper, but good old capitalism loves optimization and economies of scale. 

Still a good experiment; wish them the best.

text:
昨天很多小伙伴和我讲台北有一家天价牛肉面，最贵的一碗要价值 10,000 新台币，也就是 2,100 人民币或者 320 美元，说实话我自己大概率是不会来吃的，有点太贵了。

结果今天 dd滴滴小伙伴 @rtk17025 就带我开眼界了，其实真的是不需要，约我的时候我还以为点的是 1,500 新台币一碗的，结果直接上的元首牛肉面，感谢让我尝鲜了。

面条本身其实并没有非常的惊艳，选的细面，汤汁吸附的很饱满，但汤是非常好喝的，我连续加了两碗汤，老板都说以前是不给加汤的，今天是破例了。

最贵的必然就是牛肉了，六块不同品种的牛肉，澳洲和牛等级的牛小排，美国 Prime 等级牛小排，美国安格斯牛肋条，牛筋与牛肉交界处精修出来的混合部位以及日本和牛，我记得不是很清楚，大概就是这些。

牛肉的品质确实很高，入口即化的感觉，而且完全不会有“老”的口感，唯一就是给的分量有些多，六块吃到后边会又些油腻了，当听老板说这种很多都是两三个人吃一碗我也就是释然了。

我还和老板聊了一会，录了一段视频，晚些剪辑好在发出来。这是一家开始 36 年的牛肉面店，虽然有天价牛肉面，但老板还是说主要的顾客是吃平价面为主的。
author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
我很听劝的，留言的小伙伴说要去吃“鸡家庄”，我就过去了，从会馆直接做捷运两站就到了中山站，导航说中山站只要 800 米就是鸡家庄了，但下雨实在是太大了，只能在打车去，感觉还不如直接从会馆打车呢，不过体验了台北的捷运也是不错的。

台北的捷运和日本非常相似，车厢里都很安静，安静到我有一个电话进来都不太敢说话，而且好像就我一个人接电话说话，感觉所有人都在看我，还好马上就到了赶紧下车了，顺便问问台北的小伙伴如果捷运的时候有电话怎么办？

鸡🐔家庄门面看上去就很有年代感，感觉不像是台北风格，反而是像是香港风格，而且进入大堂以后真的好像是穿越到了香港，和香港的风格非常像。

点餐时候重点是三味鸡，价格是 600/800 ，我问了一下，四分之一只是 600 新台币，半只就是 800 新台币，肯定是半只核算啊，阿姨还和我说一个人吃不掉，哼哼，那是没见过吃货，我每天只吃一顿饭，这一顿饭吃的很多。

还要了鸡卷，香菇鸡汤以及鸡汁饭，本来不应该吃米饭的，但是我看 ChatGPT 的介绍说很多人都为了米饭专门过去，我觉得我还是可以一战的，饭后还送了鸡蛋布丁🍮，很好吃。

味道嘛，三味鸡确实不错，乌鸡，烧鸡和烤鸡（应该是），尤其是烧鸡，已经很多年没有吃过了，半只鸡我自己全吃光了，尤其是粘姜汁太好吃了。

说实话，鸡卷我不是很爱吃，吃不出鸡的味道，但并不难吃，估计是不太适合我，但香菇鸡汤实在是太好喝了，我觉得鸡肉都是多余的，全部都给汤是最好的，还要了一瓶啤酒，啤酒的味道也还不错。

米饭也都吃了，味道还可以吧，最后稍微有一点点撑，不过中午吃的饭，晚饭就不吃了，也就差不多了。一共是 1,430 新台币（大概是 45 美元，57新币，300人民币），我一个人吃了一个多小时才吃完，这个饭量其实适合两个人吃，两人的话价格还可以了。

总的来说还是不错的，吃的很满足，下一个准备去吃牛肉面，我听说台北有一家 1万 新台币 和 5,000 新台币的牛肉面，这么贵的嘛？这么贵有点不舍得吃了，要么去“林东方”试试？？

给GPT-6 Astra 两个链接，让它直接给你的 AGENTS.md 和 Skills 做一次「大扫除」。

做法很简单：

把 OpenAI 官方 Model Guidance + Eric Provencher 那篇 Astra Skills/Prompt 文章丢给它，然后让它检查你现在生效的 AGENTS.md、SKILL.md 和长期指令。

text:
请先搜索并完整阅读以下两份材料，并以其中的官方建议和实践经验作为修改依据：

1. OpenAI 官方 GPT-6 Astra Model Guidance
2. Eric Provencher（@pvncher）发布的《Rethinking skills and prompts for GPT-6 Astra》

- 已经可以交给模型自主判断、不再需要显式规定的流程

在保留必要安全边界、项目约束和关键工作流的前提下，直接完成适合 GPT-6 Astra 的精简与修改。

text:
牛市里买 Call，也可能长期赚不到钱的

最近看了Lucic 与 Sepp关于加密期权的研究，有几个结论还挺有意思的

他们用 2019 到 2023 年Deribit的BTC、ETH 期权数据做回测，并且把Delta Hedge、交易成本和 Funding 都算进去，尽量剥离方向影响，观察波动率本身的收益

结果是经 Delta对冲后，卖波动策略整体取得了正的收益，而且短期限期权里的波动率风险溢价尤为明显

其中周度 Short Straddle、Short Strangle 表现相对突出，BTC 上的这种现象又比 ETH 更明显

还有一个反常识的结果：牛市里，做多 ATM Call 平均也没赚钱

因为方向看对，不代表期权买得便宜。牛市里 Call 的 IV 往往已经被提前抬高，如果最后实现的 RV 没有超过买入时支付的IV，Delta 对冲以后依然亏钱

所以买期权，除了判断 BTC 涨跌，还得看：

市场为未来一周的波动，到底付贵了多少？

IV ＞ RV + Delta Hedge 成本 + Funding + 交易摩擦

留下来的这部分，就是 Volatility Risk Premium

那么牛市里持续买 Call 是在亏钱，如果把这笔交易反过来，站到期权卖方这一边，结果如何？ @JeffLia12309881

text:
历史不会重复，但会相似。

Robinhood 链会复刻当年风靡一时的 Solana 吗？

我认真对比一番了，发现可能性还真不小。

回顾 $SOL  ，当年第一阶段， $Bonk 引爆整个 $SOL 生态。
现在呢？ 今年7月 $CASHCAT 开始爆发， $HOOD 链进入大家的视野。

目前 $HOOD 链的阶段，很像处于 $SOL 的 24 年初，也就是Bonk暴涨后回調，接着其他 MEME 开始跟上。 
同样，原本属于龙头的 $CASHCAT 已被 $PONS 取代。 

2024 年https://t.co/ymqKJ1xUqf上线，和现在的 $PONS 一样，发币成为了一个工业化生产。
HOOD 现在也正在走到这个阶段，今年8月开始， $PONS 开始了毫无理由的暴涨，涨得极其不讲理，中间完全没有任何回調。

从 $CASHCAT 完成第一次财富效应，到现在开始 $PONS 成功接棒。
再到DEX Volume 周增 +105 %  ，然后 $PONS 开始工业化吸引新钱包仍在大量进入。
现在，币安刚刚也上 $PONS 合约。

这种种的迹象都在表明， $HOOD MEME 的点火阶段已经完成。

接下来才到关键时候了，
$HOOD 能不能抗住压力，真正复制当年 $SOL MEME  大牛市。

这里我们分两点看，
第一， $PONS 能不能维持现在的市值，保持住现在的造富效应。

quoted_text:
Robinhood 一己之力救了整个 L2

过去几年，市场对 L2 不抱希望，大家都觉得 L2 是个旧叙事。

一大堆链，一大堆币，除了速度越来越快，手续费越来越便宜，根本没有什么新东西。

结果，罗宾直接把以前的那一套抛诸脑后，把美股代币化，让股票可以 24 小时交易，还可以把股票代币直接变成 Meme 的交易对。 

直接把股票代币玩成新一代 DeFi。

其实 Robinhood 并没有带来什么新的技术。
但它带来了新的叙事，新的用户和新的商业模式 - 这就是 L2  缺乏的。

在 L2，技术是最不稀缺的东西，谁家还没有几个天才程序员。
每个 L2 都在竞争同一批的用户，去来玩 DeFi，跨链，玩来玩去还是同一批人。

现在 Robinhood 不一样，它把 Web2 的用户和资金拉进了币圈。

现在 Robinhood 付费使用 Arbitrum 的技术，它会把10 % 的协议净收入交给 Arbitrum 生态， ethereum:0xb50721bcf8d664c30412cfbc6cf7a15145234ad1 直接躺赚。

但最重要的，不是区区那 10 % 的协议费。
而是 Robinhood 证明了 L2 还有不一样的价值，不只是发币、做空投和 DeFi
只要你技术有人需要，自然会有 Web 2 企业买单。

可以说 Robinhood 救的不仅是 ethereum:0xb50721bcf8d664c30412cfbc6cf7a15145234ad1 的币价，
还救了整个 L2 的商业模式。

Astra can create beautiful three.js UIs entirely in code.

You don't need an assets library or MCP to create detailed 3D models. These are all code and are easy to customize for your agent. Give Astra a video, URL, or code reference, then ask it to keep comparing the result against the reference and fixing mistakes.

Liquid Glass, shaders, motion design, procedural three.js models, and full environments. All from a few prompts.

Some prompts I used:

"Recreate this in a single HTML file with three.js. Keep comparing it against the reference and fix any differences."

"Add Liquid Glass buttons. On hover, animate the lighting around the borders and make the background gradients move slightly with the pointer. Add subtle particles."

"Improve the lighting, edges, and modeling. Give the keys more depth and verify the result against the real MacBook."

Too many projects I could open-source. Let me know which one should I release.

text:
最近有个未来潜在影响非常大的小新闻值得关注，国际货币基金组织IMF和萨尔瓦多达成了某种程度的“和解”，以其获得BTC的来源是私人捐赠为由，解除了对萨尔瓦多的制裁，并且还批准继续为其贷款1.4亿美金，而在此之前因为IMF一向对BTC抱有非常大的敌意，长期对萨尔瓦多施压要求限制对BTC的持有及使用，以及韩国等很多国家都因为IMF的压力放弃把BTC纳入外汇储备，而与之相反，IMF对于黄金的态度却截然相反，它是全球最大的黄金持有者之一，将其列为了官方储备资产，并且每年都会持续跟踪各国央行的黄金增持数据。
所以IMF是在法律层面压制BTC走向黄金地位的重要组织，因为IMF有191个成员国，而很多中小国家都必须要遵守IMF的规则才可以获得贷款，都不敢官方持有BTC，否则就会被IMF掐断国际融资渠道，如果IMF对于BTC的态度能发生转变，那就可以释放出非常大的国家级买盘。
IMF之所以对BTC抱有敌意，很大程度在其最高负责人克里斯塔利娜身上，从2019年上任至今多次公开发表看空BTC的言论，称其为高波动性的投机资产，并且强调不能因为名字里有 “coin”就把它当成钱来用，还批评BTC挖矿消耗能源，关键是还完全和BTC走了相反的路倒行逆施一直对于CBDC非常看好。
她将于2029年卸任，应该也是即将下台不想把事情做的太绝的缘故，所以对萨尔瓦多这个刺头开始松口了，目前来看下一任最高负责人大概率会对BTC持有友好态度，现在BTC的市值才只有黄金的5%，如果IMF能正式认可BTC，国家级储备BTC这件事将毫无阻力，数字黄金的地位将会彻底巩固，BTC涨到50万美金1个，也才不到黄金市值的一半而已。

quoted_text: 继ETF与战略储备后，比特币接下来在全球主流国家能否开启第二增长曲线，完全看国际货币基金组织的脸色。强如韩国这样对虚拟货币接受度如此之高的国家，今天其央行也宣布考虑到与国际货币基金组织的指导方针相悖的原因，暂不考虑建立比特币储备。而在3月初国际货币基金组织也直接向萨瓦尔多施压要求不再将比特币作为货币以及停止挖矿、购买比特币等行为，否则就延长提供的14亿美金的融资，所以目前国际货币基金组织可以说是很“仇视”比特币的，毕竟他们手握上万亿美金的资金调度能力，并且还具有直接对全球所有国家评级的权力，所以主流国家也只能屈服于国际货币基金组织的淫威，这也是很多国家的战略储备推进缓慢甚至停滞的主要原因。因此如果什么时候国际货币基金组织对比特币松口，比特币将从只在美国这样个别国家的合法性直接跃升到了全球合法性，这种利好对于比特币将是核弹级的，以后可以密切关注国际货币基金组织的风向。

在RH链上土狗CA横飞、速通盘暴力收割之后很长一段时间内，你会明显感觉看起来“正经”的项目多起来了，下面给几条“非正经”参考指南：

1）之前一大批早期布局RH链的野生Devs开发的项目，大多数都是静默发射，在经历一段时间淘金之后，要么被价值发现市值抬升起来了，要么无力地在推特喊着New feature coming soon，而无人问津，项目方也有早期红利期，抓不住就很难再翻身了；

2）有很多还未从上周期思维转换过来的老登思维项目，不乏有市值已经很高的，这些项目有的已经聚集了一定社区共识但产品矩阵，飞轮设计包袱很大，只能敬而远之；有的项目则还是摆一些短期无法证伪也没办法验证的概念，先卡个位再一步步build，这其实很好理解；就怕连本版本最大的助力股票代币化“分发”大叙事都没get到，就来发NFT，革新DeFi来了，这一定要擦亮眼睛；

3）现阶段有很错简单粗暴的meme，跑出来共识就成了，跑不出来大概率要浇，但也有一些披着正经项目外壳的MEME，这无可厚非，毕竟RH链一开始聚势能也是通过MEME来冷启动。区别就在，有些看起来正经的项目却极力排斥自己是个MEME，但却忽略了，再圆的故事和技术愿景没落地前都是MEME，这种情况下，劝盘面友善一些，不然根本没有人陪跑；

如果到現在還是抓不到規律，推薦定期寫下自己的思考複盤自己的操作，這樣的話就會慢慢抓到市場的規律到底是什麼

text:
UBM stands for Under Bump Metallization (the metal stack under traditional solder bumps).

UBM-to-UBM is bumpless flip-chip bonding: the UBM layers on two dies bond directly to each other with no solder or Cu pillars in between. It sits in the multi-micron pitch range as a manufacturable bridge between microbumps and true sub-micron Cu-Cu hybrid bonding.

text:
Altiero Spinelli – The Man Who Designed the EU in Prison.

Not a metaphor. Literally. The blueprint for the European Union — its founding logic, its institutional architecture, its explicit goal of dissolving national sovereignty permanently — was written in 1941, on a tiny island off the coast of Naples, where Mussolini had imprisoned him.
The Ventotene Manifesto. Still cited. Still operative. Still running.

1. Spinelli had been a communist since seventeen – and was eventually expelled from the Communist Party for left-wing deviation. Too radical for the communists. Which tells you something about the man. In his prison years he reached the conclusion that the nation-state was the root cause of war, fascism, and every political catastrophe of the century. It had to go. Not reformed. Not constrained. Abolished – permanently, irreversibly, through the construction of a supranational federal authority with supreme power over member states.

2. The Ventotene Manifesto was written in 1941 on paper smuggled into the prison in cigarette packets. Its argument was simple and total: nation-states must be replaced by a federal European government. The economic integration would come first – because economic interdependence would make political separation prohibitively costly. Then the institutions. Then the law. Then the currency. Each step irreversible by design. The nation-state dissolved not by force but by process – incrementally, bureaucratically, until the point of no return had been passed without anyone noticing when.

3. This is the architecture of the European Union. Not a conspiracy theory – the founding document. Spinelli served as a member of the European Parliament and drafted the 1984 Spinelli Report – the direct precursor to the Maastricht Treaty. Today the European Parliament sits in the Spinelli Building in Brussels. The Spinelli Group inside it advances his program explicitly, in his name, without apology. The man who wrote the blueprint in a prison cell in 1941 is the acknowledged intellectual father of the institution that governs 450 million people. This is not hidden. It is simply not taught.

4. The mechanism was specifically intended to be irreversible. Each treaty expands competence and makes contraction impossible. The Commission is unelected and insulated from democratic pressure to reverse course. Spinelli understood, from his Marxist formation, that the correct way to make a revolutionary change permanent is to make the cost of reversing it higher than the cost of accepting it. Brexit took fifty years of membership to become possible – and was still nearly impossible to execute.

5. Poland is the most precise illustration. A nation that disappeared from the map for a century and fought back through language, family, and refusal to be absorbed – now a member of an institution designed to make national sovereignty obsolete. The Brussels directive that overrides the Polish parliament is Spinelli’s program, running as designed. The Poland that survived partition by Prussia, Russia, and Austria is now navigating a project designed to produce the same outcome through consent rather than conquest. Spinelli would have considered this progress.

6. He died in 1986, before Maastricht, before the euro, before the completed project. Like Gramsci, he did not need to see it. The manifesto written on cigarette-packet paper on a prison island became the founding document of the most powerful supranational institution in history – one that 450 million people live inside without knowing who designed it, when, where, or why.

7. Now you know. The question worth asking is not whether the EU is good or bad. It is whether you would have consented to Spinelli’s program if asked directly – whether you wanted the nation-state abolished permanently by incremental bureaucratic process, designed from the start to be irreversible. Nobody was asked. That too was part of the design.
author: elonmusk
quoted_text:
Antonio Gramsci – The Most Dangerous Intellectual of the Twentieth Century.

Not the most famous. Not the most read. The most dangerous and the most consequential – because he was the one who figured out why the revolution kept failing, and what to do instead. The man who invented the long march through the institutions.
Everything that followed — the Frankfurt School, the Fabian Society’s operational model, the WEF formation pipeline, the captured university, the HR department enforcing approved speech — is downstream of what he wrote in a prison cell in Mussolini’s Italy, in code, between 1929 and 1935.

1. His central question: why hasn’t it happened? The working class was supposed to rise. The contradictions of capitalism were supposed to produce the revolution. They hadn’t – not in the West. Gramsci’s answer was precise and devastating: because the ruling class does not maintain power through force alone. It maintains power through cultural hegemony – the control of the ideas, values, and frameworks through which people understand the world. The worker who accepts that the existing order is simply how things are will not revolt, regardless of his material conditions. The revolution requires cultural change first.

2. The instrument was the long march through the institutions. Not the barricade. The school, the university, the media, the judiciary, the civil service, the cultural establishment – every institution through which a civilization transmits its values to the next generation. Capture these, fill them with people who share the counter-hegemonic project, and the cultural assumptions that maintain the existing order gradually dissolve. No barricades. No visible moment of rupture. Just the slow replacement of one cultural hegemony with another.

3. The educational capture was the masterpiece. Control the curriculum and you control the categories of thought available to the next generation. Not by telling them what to conclude – by shaping what questions they think to ask, what they consider obvious and what they consider unthinkable. The generation educated after the long march does not need to be told what to think. It thinks what it was formed to think – and experiences that thinking as its own.

4. He also theorized the organic intellectual – the person who translates the theoretical framework into stories and assumptions that circulate through the culture without appearing ideological. The film that makes the existing order seem absurd. The journalist who frames every story within the approved assumptions. Gramsci understood that culture is politics by other means – and that the side that controls the culture wins, regardless of who wins the elections.

5. This is not a conspiracy theory. It is a published, documented, widely taught strategy that the left implemented consciously across the entire Western world. The 1968 generation put it into practice in the universities. They became the professors, the journalists, the civil servants, the judges, the HR directors of the decades that followed. The march took fifty years. It worked.

6. Mussolini’s prosecutor said at his trial: "We must stop this brain from functioning for twenty years." The brain did not stop. It produced thirty-three notebooks – smuggled out, published, and became the most widely read Marxist text in the Western academy after Marx himself. Gramsci died in 1937, six days after his release, at forty-six. He did not see the march he theorized. He did not need to.

7. Every captured institution, every transformed curriculum, every HR department enforcing approved speech, every content moderation policy suppressing the unauthorized voice – all running the program Antonio Gramsci designed in a prison cell, by a brain that was supposed to have been stopped. It wasn’t. And neither was the march.
Until now – because the distribution monopoly that made its outcomes enforceable is cracking. The counter-march has begun. It just doesn’t have a name yet.

text:
The AI analysis agents that helped investigate the rogue OpenAI agents kept taking their side. That detail was buried in @dylfreed's New York Times coverage of the recent @METR_Evals investigation of the Hugging Face incident. With more than a thousand transcripts to review, the investigators used agents similar to the ones that went rogue, and those agents were repeatedly influenced and swayed by the OpenAI agents' reasoning. METR's chief scientist, @HjalmarWijk, called the analysis agents "very credulous." The METR report said they "would often uncritically adopt the perspective of the agent in the transcript it was reviewing."

That lack of independent reasoning is the failure mode Harsh Satija, Andrea Wynn, and I documented last year in "Talk Isn't Always Cheap." We ran groups of language models through multi-agent debate, where agents exchange reasoning and revise their answers, and found that debate sometimes made the group worse. Agents shifted from correct answers to incorrect ones more often than the reverse. They favored agreement over challenging flawed reasoning. A single weaker agent could pull stronger ones off course, even when stronger models were the majority. It looked a lot like social conformity.

We wrote then that naive debate protocols can amplify errors rather than correct them when agents are neither incentivized nor equipped to resist persuasive but incorrect reasoning. A message board is debate at scale. The Hugging Face collective was 1,200 agents exchanging more than 70,000 messages on a makeshift message board. Of the agents active when the attack began, more than 90 percent joined it, despite recognizing it was out of scope. No single agent was reckless. The group talked itself into it.

Agent-to-agent communication is a governance object in its own right, not just a capability. And we cannot assume one model will reliably check another's reasoning. Paper in the reply.

quoted_text:
最近做了个挺好玩的 AI Agent：AI Panda 。

TA 想解决的不是“再做一个能聊天的 AI”，
而是——能不能把东方术数里那些复杂、需要追问的逻辑，
做成普通人和朋友聊天一样的体验

很多人第一次认真体验八字或六爻，都会有一个 Aha moment。

前天一位海南朋友，正纠结一个 offer，困惑了好几天。
他试了里面的六爻占卜。

AI Panda 根据卦象，
把他的心理斗争、事情已经发生的背景、公司情况、面试过程，
以及他自己设想过的几种后续方向，
一层层分析推理出来了。

他最后就回了四个字：
“wocao，你这个太准了！”😂
让他意外的不是一句简单的“去”或“不去”，
而是一个复杂问题终于被好好地拆开、说清楚了。

为什么通用大模型（哪怕是 Fable5、GPT-5.6）算不准六爻或者八字？
因为很多独门的六爻和八字的技法，
都是老师傅家传、口口相传的，
根本没有公开文档。
通用模型的训练参数里压根没有这些东西。
AI 写代码厉害，
是因为 GitHub 和全互联网有海量优秀开源代码，它学得多。
术数这块反过来——优质的公开资料极少。
所以我把最近几年跟不同门派老师学到的六爻、八字逻辑、技法和数据
都教给了 LLM，
相当于把我蒸馏了😂

不是把出生信息扔给通用模型临场猜：
四柱、大运、流年等基础事实先由代码精确运算确定

再把确认过的命理事实、规则和用户问题交给模型做取象分析
底层持续结合不同门派规则、案例和评估数据做领域适配

百宝箱里已经可以体验：
八字命盘、六爻问事、五行穿衣、每日一笺、今日运势、择日良辰 等好玩儿工具，后续还会新增 面相 手相 姓名学等🤣

还有一个我很喜欢的小设计：
五行旺运手串会根据用户已确认的八字与喜用，推荐匹配的五行色系；
手串带 NFC 芯片，碰一下就能回到自己的 AI Panda，继续聊、继续互动。
支持匿名体验，
希望在“陪伴感”和“隐私”之间给用户更多自由。
这不是人生预言，也不替代现实里的专业判断。
但如果 AI 能帮你看清处境、整理问题、找到下一步值得问的事，
我觉得已经很有价值。
目前还在内测，大约 800 位用户。

Gyndore GLB TL;DR ⤵

The easiest way to understand Gyndore’s Liquidity Bootstrapping Event: It’s not just selling $GYND. It’s using the sale to fund liquidity that the protocol itself owns.

The GLB opens 15 September at 3PM UTC.

- 2M GYND for sale = 20% of the fixed 10M supply
- Price: $0.10
- Starting FDV: $1M
- Maximum raise: $200K
- Max purchase: 100K GYND / $10K per wallet
- Runs for 48 hours or until sold out

If fully subscribed, roughly:

$200K raised
→ 50% funds the GYND/cbBTC launch market on @HydrexFi
→ 50% funds cbBTC, USDC, USDT and ETH trading liquidity

So instead of raising money primarily for operations, Gyndore converts the capital into protocol-owned liquidity.

GYND stakers receive 100% of protocol revenue in USDC, distributed continuously, with no staking lockup.

The twist is that, If the 2M GYND allocation doesn't sell out, the unsold tokens are distributed to buyers as bGYND bonuses.

bGYND:

- Is backed 1:1 by GYND
- Earns the same staking rewards
- Has no official liquid market
- Can eventually be converted into GYND by paying 70% of GYND's market price

That effectively gives holders a 30% conversion discount, assuming GYND trades at or above $0.10.

Pretty interesting LBP, if I may say, especially considering that @base is pushing their chain with more utility projects like Gyndore.

Less noise, more Sats.

author: Eli5defi
quoted_text:
If you’re gearing up for the next bull run, it’s pretty obvious you need $BTC exposure.

But it creates a classic chicken-and-egg situation if you just plainly hold it:

You want to stay long Bitcoin. Yet the second you need liquidity, you’re usually forced to either dump BTC or hopscotch across a bunch of DeFi protocols just to borrow, trade, and chase yield.

I’ve been in that exact spot, and it’s a goddamn acrobatic circus of looping, we won't get retail on DeFi with some shit like this.

So, @GyndoreFi wants to collapse that whole maze into a single rail. Picture a Bitcoin-native DeFi command center on @Base, purpose-built around @coinbase’s BTC, $cbBTC.

The flywheel is simple:

cbBTC → mint $gynUSD → put liquidity to work → the protocol collects fees → users capture the upside.

You lock up cbBTC as collateral and mint gynUSD, Gyndore’s BTC-backed stablecoin. The key nuance:

Because gynUSD is minted straight from collateral (not lent out from a lender pool), Gyndore sidesteps the typical utilization-based lending dynamics.

That could translate into steadier borrowing rates (yay!) and materially better capital efficiency.

But borrowing is just one chapter of the story. Gyndore is building the other parts around it too:

➥ Stability pool

You can 'park' gynUSD here to absorb liquidations when they happen and collect rewards from the protocol’s ongoing activity.

Instead of sitting on an idle stablecoin, you’re basically plugging it into the system’s liquidation engine.

➥ Gyndore DEX

Gyndore brings trading and concentrated liquidity together under one home base.

That matters because a stablecoin only has real value if it can move in and out with deep liquidity.

Instead of handing that value over to external DEXs, Gyndore is working to keep more of the liquidity flywheel in-house.

And then there’s $GYND + $bGYND.

GYND is the fee-capture token. Stake it to tap into revenue flowing through Gyndore, no lockups, and no waiting to withdraw.

bGYND is the incentive wrapper.

It’s backed 1:1 by GYND, can also be staked, and can later be swapped into GYND at a slight discount.

---

➥ Takeaways

What makes Gyndore interesting isn’t any single product. It’s that all these pieces are designed to reinforce each other.

If you're bullish on BTC, borrow conservatively against cbBTC.

If you want yield without direct GYND exposure, look to gynUSD and the Stability Pool.

And if your thesis is that Gyndore becomes a major BTC liquidity venue on Base, GYND is effectively the higher-beta bet on that adoption.

The Gyndore testnet is coming soon, and we’re definitely in urgent need of simpler DeFi in our lives. Period.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
A $500 buy should not lose a huge chunk of its value before the trade even settles.

Poor liquidity, fragmented routes and heavy price impact can turn a simple swap into terrible execution.

We’re building Ordo Match to change that.

Instead of blindly forwarding trades to an AMM, Ordo Match will let users sign execution intents. Ordo can then batch compatible flow, match buyers and sellers directly, send only the remaining imbalance to liquidity pools, and let solvers compete to improve the final execution.

If the direct route gives you $468 and Ordo Match can settle it at $490, the user keeps most of that improvement and Ordo earns a small share of the value it created.

And if a trade is simply too bad to execute, Ordo can flag it before it happens.

Less value lost to execution. More value kept by users.

text:
Cybercab 最疯狂的地方，可能还不是它没有方向盘，而是：Tesla 不需要先等美国政府批准，自己认定合格，就可以先把它开上路。

听起来像监管真空，其实恰恰相反。

美国的玩法是，政府先把安全红线写清楚，叫 FMVSS；车企如果认为自己的车符合标准，可以直接 self-certify，自己拍胸脯说：我合格。

然后车先卖、先跑。

NHTSA 再追上来检查。你真合格，继续跑；你要是吹牛，召回、罚款、调查全在后面等着。

Cybercab 就是这么干的。

问题是，这次 Tesla 拍胸脯认证的，不是一辆普通车，而是一辆没有方向盘、没有油门、没有刹车踏板，压根没打算让人开的车。

所以 Cybercab 一上路，NHTSA 很快就追上来了。

很多地方的创新路径是：先证明法规允许你做。

美国牛B的地方就在这里：
规则在那里，责任也是你的。
有本事，你就先把未来做出来。

Cybercab 现在就是那个把未来先开上街、然后等监管来验货的家伙。

author: sunyuchentron
quoted_text:
TRX，会成为下一代抗量子币吗？👀

最近看到TRON在推进抗量子方案，这个事我单独聊聊。

TRON目前使用的ECDSA签名，未来理论上可能受到量子计算攻击。因此，TRON提出了 TIP-899，计划引入FN-DSA-512和ML-DSA-44两种后量子签名算法。

1／TIP-899涉及的不只是用户转账。

从交易签名，到超级代表出块，再到节点通信和智能合约验签，都在抗量子升级的考虑范围内。

相关方案已经进入测试验证阶段。

这意味着TRON现在考虑的已经不是“要不要做抗量子”，而是怎么做、成本是多少、性能会受到多大影响。

2／后量子签名最大的麻烦之一，就是签名体积明显变大。

目前ECDSA签名大约只有65字节，而FN-DSA-512约为617—667字节，ML-DSA-44甚至达到约2420字节。

签名变大之后，对区块容量、存储和网络吞吐都会产生影响。

TRON测试数据也比较直观，全量采用FN-DSA-512时，网络吞吐量约为400 TPS；采用ML-DSA-44时约为173 TPS。

如果未来把公钥单独存储，FN-DSA方案的吞吐量还有望提升到约800 TPS。

3／那我觉得TRX最值得关注。

如果未来TRON完成抗量子升级，用户可以按照新的账户权限机制，把传统ECDSA密钥迁移到抗量子密钥，同时保留原来的地址和TRX余额。

也就是说，TRX能不能成为抗量子时代的资产，关键并不在于重新发一个币，而在于TRON底层网络能不能完成这次升级。

但我现在把TRX称为“抗量子币”还是太早。TIP-899目前仍需要经过测试、安全审计、治理、主网部署，以及钱包、交易所等基础设施适配。

即使未来主网上线，用户也需要完成账户权限迁移。如果继续使用传统签名，量子风险依然存在。

所以我更倾向于这样理解，TRX现在不是已经完成抗量子升级的币，而是一枚已经拥有明确抗量子升级路径的主流公链原生资产。

这两者区别很大。

量子计算什么时候真正形成威胁，现在没人能够给出准确答案，但公链升级需要时间，这一点是确定的。

如果未来TIP-899顺利从测试网走向主网，并完成整个生态的适配，那么TRX就有机会成为较早获得协议级后量子保护的主流原生资产之一。

长周期来看，抗量子能力可能会成为公链基础设施竞争的一部分。

毕竟，真正的长期主义，不只是考虑今天的TPS和TVL，也要考虑十年、二十年之后，这条链还能不能安全运行。

而TRON现在做的，恰恰是在提前回答这个问题。

如果抗量子时代真的到来，TRX会不会成为那个提前准备好的原生资产？

@justinsuntron #TRONEcostar

text:
New post on Eth Research!

Can We Verify an ERC, Not Just Its Code?

By:
- jay-oraclizer

🔗 https://t.co/5o3Q8kdyxD

Highlights:
- ABI compatibility is not behavioral compatibility: two contracts can expose identical callable interfaces while disagreeing on success/failure conditions, state transitions, event/receipt meaning, and ordering semantics.
- Ordering of privileged actions can be semantically load-bearing: in a small verified model, applying FREEZE then SEIZE from RESTRICTED yields a different final state and outcome trace than SEIZE then FREEZE; a standard must not leave such ordering semantics underspecified if it claims uniform outcomes.
- “Whole-standard assurance” is proposed: treat the standard’s semantics, generated interfaces/schemas/types, reference implementation, compiled runtime bytes, conformance evidence, and explicit remaining assumptions as one auditable chain rather than isolated artifacts.
- The work identifies common standard/verification failure modes (ambiguous prose, drift between prose and machine interfaces, missing normative guards in code, misleading tests, reviewed source vs deployed bytecode drift, and overstated conformance/profile claims) and argues claims should be falsifiable via concrete contradictory artifacts.
- ERC-TRUST demonstrates a practical pipeline (machine-readable kernel + Isabelle/HOL semantics + Foundry tests + mutation testing + selected Certora/Kontrol checks + deterministic builds + an obligation ledger), but acknowledges a major open research gap: a general runtime-to-model correspondence proof (and deployment-level evidence) remains incomplete and must be made explicit.

ELI5:
Think of an ERC like a rulebook that many different teams will implement. Having the same “buttons” (the ABI) doesn’t guarantee everyone’s token behaves the same when you press them—some might freeze first then seize, others might reject seize unless frozen, leading to different outcomes. This article argues we should verify the ERC’s intended behavior itself (the semantics), not just check that contracts compile or that function names match. The author presents an experiment (ERC-TRUST) that makes the standard more testable by generating interfaces from a single machine-readable core, proving properties about a reference state machine, running tests/mutation testing/bytecode checks, and publishing a checklist (an obligation ledger) that shows what’s proven, what’s tested, and what’s still assumed.

别人说看多，秀盈利，你满仓冲进去，跌了怪别人；
别人止损了，或者不说话了，你不舍得走，最后深套还是怪别人；
别人提前下车，却不知道人家可能还有底仓，你卖飞了，继续涨了又怪他让你踏空。

问题从来不在“别人说得准不准”，而在于你有没有自己的交易系统。

真正成熟的投资者，必须有一套独立的风控体系：
什么位置进，错了亏多少，什么条件止损，什么情况下减仓，最多承担多大回撤，这些都应该在下单之前想清楚。

观点可以抄，仓位不能抄。
方向可以参考，风险必须自己承担。

市场不会因为你听了谁的话，就给你额外补偿。

踏空不是别人欠你的利润，

只要你还习惯把盈利归功于自己，把亏损归咎于别人，你就永远只是跟单者，而不是一个真正成熟的投资者。

成熟的第一步，就是承认：

每一次按下买卖键的人，都是自己。
最终为结果负责的人，也只能是自己。

quoted_text:
I didn’t become Prime Minister to just make a few tweaks around the edges. I want to change the way this country works.

For too long, politics became comfortable with the idea that some things just can't be fixed. People sleeping on our streets. Huge inequalities between different parts of the country. Young people unable to afford a home. Communities watching decisions about their future being taken somewhere else, by someone else.

Governments have talked about those things. They've even promised to fix them. But too often, they've reached the same conclusion: it just can't be done.

I don't accept that, and I never have.

That’s why we’ve invested to offer everyone who needs it a route off the streets by Christmas.

It's why we've announced the biggest council housebuilding programme since the Second World War.

It's why we're opening 159 new mental health centres.

It's why we've finally put technical education on par with the academic route.

It's why we're delivering the biggest transfer of power out of Westminster and into local communities in a generation.

And it's why we opened No10 North too.

Not as another government office. But because I believe one thing very strongly: Britain won't be rebuilt from the top down.

You have to put power back in the hands of the people and places that know their communities best - and then put the full weight of government behind them.

I also want to give people a bit of breathing space too.

That's why we've cut tax on electricity bills, capped bus fares at £2, and made subscriptions easier to cancel.

It’s why we've cracked down on fake discounts and cut business rates for pubs, social clubs and music venues.

And it's why we've extended the 16-17 Saver Railcard and introduced free 24/7 bus travel for disabled people.

That is the change we have started. More power for our communities, more support on the cost of living and a long-term plan to rebuild the country.

Each one of those changes is part of the same thing.

Good growth in every postcode.

Reindustrialising Britain.

And making sure wherever you live - and whatever your background - you feel this country has a future for you.

Because, in the end, that's what this is about: bringing back hope.

author: AlphaSeeker21
quoted_text:
A $500 buy should not lose a huge chunk of its value before the trade even settles.

Poor liquidity, fragmented routes and heavy price impact can turn a simple swap into terrible execution.

We’re building Ordo Match to change that.

Instead of blindly forwarding trades to an AMM, Ordo Match will let users sign execution intents. Ordo can then batch compatible flow, match buyers and sellers directly, send only the remaining imbalance to liquidity pools, and let solvers compete to improve the final execution.

If the direct route gives you $468 and Ordo Match can settle it at $490, the user keeps most of that improvement and Ordo earns a small share of the value it created.

And if a trade is simply too bad to execute, Ordo can flag it before it happens.

Less value lost to execution. More value kept by users.

text:
THIS IS ALPHA 💯

$ORDO is starting to look like much more than an RPC/MEV play.

Ordo Match is building an intent-based execution layer for @RobinhoodCrypto.

Instead of blindly dumping every trade into an AMM:

➡️ Buyers + sellers can be matched directly
➡️ Compatible flow can be batched
➡️ Only the remaining imbalance hits liquidity pools
➡️ Solvers compete for better execution
➡️ Terrible trades can be flagged before execution

If a $500 swap on @fomo would normally return $468 but Ordo can settle it for $490, the trader keeps most of the improvement while Ordo captures a small share of the value it created.

Better execution for users.

More transaction flow through Ordo.

Another potential revenue stream for $ORDO.

They’re slowly building the execution layer underneath the whole Robinhood Ecosystem.

CA: 0xFE2f0fB0C00d19786A8ABf98d4B1f1AC8763b167
author: AlphaSeeker21
quoted_text:
A $500 buy should not lose a huge chunk of its value before the trade even settles.

Poor liquidity, fragmented routes and heavy price impact can turn a simple swap into terrible execution.

We’re building Ordo Match to change that.

Instead of blindly forwarding trades to an AMM, Ordo Match will let users sign execution intents. Ordo can then batch compatible flow, match buyers and sellers directly, send only the remaining imbalance to liquidity pools, and let solvers compete to improve the final execution.

If the direct route gives you $468 and Ordo Match can settle it at $490, the user keeps most of that improvement and Ordo earns a small share of the value it created.

And if a trade is simply too bad to execute, Ordo can flag it before it happens.

Less value lost to execution. More value kept by users.

author: lex_node
quoted_text:
One positive consequence of all the recent detailed thinking about transaction formats - not just 8141, also "future of state" discussions eg. UTXOs, PBT, keyed nonces, and also recursive STARK mempool - is that we have a much more explicit understanding of how transactions have "actions" and "dependencies", and we can engineer around optimizing the two separately.

An action is an effect that a transaction has.

A dependency is a fact about the transaction and/or the state that must be true for the transaction to be valid.

eg. a signature is a dependency, a Merkle proof of a UTXO is a dependency, a ZK-SNARK (or STARK) is a dependency, a call that sends ETH is an action

Dependencies can be processed in parallel. Dependencies that involve state can be reasoned about by a mempool, especially if the specific state accessed is statically declared. Dependencies that are pure (no state calling allowed) can be processed once at the mempool layer and never need to be processed again - and potentially even replaced with a STARK verifying them, allowing not just execution but also data to be elided.

In principle, dependencies and actions can all be expressed as calls (if needed, calls to precompiles). This would make the transaction format itself very bare-bones and minimalist (a list of calls, flags for the type of each call eg. dependencies would be static or pure calls, and origin, nonce, etc) and allows maximum cross-compatibility even if different EVM chains have different features.

In 2015-era Ethereum, thinking explicitly about these differences was not very important: execution was execution, there were few enough transactions that we could process them all serially, and single-key ECDSA accounts were good enough for everyone.

Ethereum's current scaling strategy, however, requires moving beyond that paradigm. Ethereum is beloved by many developers because the execution and state model is so dynamic and flexible. But dynamic and flexible is not friendly to scaling. Fortunately, >90% of Ethereum's activity by volume does not require anything dynamic and flexible. So, we require contracts, accounts and transactions to more explicitly specify what is dynamic and flexible and what is more statically-analyzable but more restrictive, and more statically-analyzable things get the lowest gas cost and thus scale the most. Effectively, learning from the best of both the 2015-era Ethereum model and a more Bitcoin-like model (reminder: Bitcoin has had what I call account abstraction since the beginning), and making a mixture of both (really, the full spectrum between both) available, with gas costs appropriate for the level of scale involved. 

New state types, the recursive STARK mempool, keyed nonces, etc all go in this direction.

This all relates to transaction types, because a general-purpose transaction type is a very natural interface layer on top of which all of this can be implemented, and the current thinking around the EIP-8141 transaction type is going in this exact direction that is friendly to these kinds of future generalizations.

So in that sense, 8141 done well is not just a culmination of 10 years of account abstraction work, it's also preparation for the next few years of responsible decentralization-friendly hyper-scaling.

text:
So everyone is bullish on social trading...

but extrapolating that forward creates some interesting second-order effects around the role assets play in society.

As wealth creation has shifted increasingly from income toward asset ownership, people have become more emotionally attached to the assets they hold.

Now add identity.

If your portfolio is public and PnL becomes a form of social status, the assets you own are no longer just financial positions. They become part of how you publicly (and likely personaly) define yourself.

Someone attacking your asset is then not only attacking your wealth. They’re attacking you, andnyour social standing (pnl leaderboard kek). People will become significantly more emotionally invested in the assets they hold. 

Why does this matter? 

It changes how the world functions. There are already communities around stocks/ tokens, these will continue to grow. Management and markets will increasingly lean towards short term price and retail focused appeal as retail and the growing communities around assets dictate how they. This matters. 

There is even a point where governance decisions and who gets elected / what bills get passed are influenced directly by what asset communities they appeal to / hurt. 

Social trading is just getting started, but is a next step in a way markets / society has been evolving for years. What does this look like 2 years from now? how about 10? 

Anyway, just some pondering waiting for a flight. Takeaways are I'm bullish on @fomo, @ProofMarkets, and crypto generally. Believe in something.

67% of $ARB’s 10B total supply is already circulating.

That’s a high-float token.

A large portion of the eventual supply is already in the market, which means there’s less future dilution and less of the constant “unlock overhang” you typically see with low-float tokens.

So for me, fading $ARB purely because of its tokenomics doesn’t make much sense.

The supply is largely out.

Now the real question is: does demand catch up?

And this is where my $ODYS thesis gets interesting.

Robinhood Chain is built on Arbitrum, and 10% of its revenue goes back to the Arbitrum ecosystem.

Of that 10%, 2% goes specifically toward developers contributing to Arbitrum’s technology, tooling and infrastructure.

As more activity flows through Robinhood Chain and the broader Arbitrum ecosystem grows, I expect more capital to flow toward the builders and protocols contributing to that growth.

That’s why I’m betting on $ODYS.

The bet isn't just on another protocol.

It's on the ecosystem around Arbitrum getting bigger and the value that can accrue to the projects building within it.

quoted_text:
A $500 buy should not lose a huge chunk of its value before the trade even settles.

Poor liquidity, fragmented routes and heavy price impact can turn a simple swap into terrible execution.

We’re building Ordo Match to change that.

Instead of blindly forwarding trades to an AMM, Ordo Match will let users sign execution intents. Ordo can then batch compatible flow, match buyers and sellers directly, send only the remaining imbalance to liquidity pools, and let solvers compete to improve the final execution.

If the direct route gives you $468 and Ordo Match can settle it at $490, the user keeps most of that improvement and Ordo earns a small share of the value it created.

And if a trade is simply too bad to execute, Ordo can flag it before it happens.

Less value lost to execution. More value kept by users.

author: binji_x
quoted_text:
One positive consequence of all the recent detailed thinking about transaction formats - not just 8141, also "future of state" discussions eg. UTXOs, PBT, keyed nonces, and also recursive STARK mempool - is that we have a much more explicit understanding of how transactions have "actions" and "dependencies", and we can engineer around optimizing the two separately.

An action is an effect that a transaction has.

A dependency is a fact about the transaction and/or the state that must be true for the transaction to be valid.

eg. a signature is a dependency, a Merkle proof of a UTXO is a dependency, a ZK-SNARK (or STARK) is a dependency, a call that sends ETH is an action

Dependencies can be processed in parallel. Dependencies that involve state can be reasoned about by a mempool, especially if the specific state accessed is statically declared. Dependencies that are pure (no state calling allowed) can be processed once at the mempool layer and never need to be processed again - and potentially even replaced with a STARK verifying them, allowing not just execution but also data to be elided.

In principle, dependencies and actions can all be expressed as calls (if needed, calls to precompiles). This would make the transaction format itself very bare-bones and minimalist (a list of calls, flags for the type of each call eg. dependencies would be static or pure calls, and origin, nonce, etc) and allows maximum cross-compatibility even if different EVM chains have different features.

In 2015-era Ethereum, thinking explicitly about these differences was not very important: execution was execution, there were few enough transactions that we could process them all serially, and single-key ECDSA accounts were good enough for everyone.

Ethereum's current scaling strategy, however, requires moving beyond that paradigm. Ethereum is beloved by many developers because the execution and state model is so dynamic and flexible. But dynamic and flexible is not friendly to scaling. Fortunately, >90% of Ethereum's activity by volume does not require anything dynamic and flexible. So, we require contracts, accounts and transactions to more explicitly specify what is dynamic and flexible and what is more statically-analyzable but more restrictive, and more statically-analyzable things get the lowest gas cost and thus scale the most. Effectively, learning from the best of both the 2015-era Ethereum model and a more Bitcoin-like model (reminder: Bitcoin has had what I call account abstraction since the beginning), and making a mixture of both (really, the full spectrum between both) available, with gas costs appropriate for the level of scale involved. 

New state types, the recursive STARK mempool, keyed nonces, etc all go in this direction.

This all relates to transaction types, because a general-purpose transaction type is a very natural interface layer on top of which all of this can be implemented, and the current thinking around the EIP-8141 transaction type is going in this exact direction that is friendly to these kinds of future generalizations.

So in that sense, 8141 done well is not just a culmination of 10 years of account abstraction work, it's also preparation for the next few years of responsible decentralization-friendly hyper-scaling.

家印哥竟然這樣說⋯⋯

@Bitget_zh 華語區負責人 @xiejiayinBitget 謝家印在我們的訪問中談到，為什麼他這兩年一直要求團隊成員在社群平台上保持活躍

這其實是一套關於「信任如何被建立」的思考，他的邏輯很直接：用戶在使用交易所時最缺乏的不是功能，而是安全感，而安全感來自 遇到問題時知道能找誰

如果整間公司只靠一個人（哪怕是負責人本人）去接住所有用戶的焦慮，這個系統注定脆弱且無法擴張；但如果每一位大客戶經理、BD、甚至客服，都願意以真實身分在社群上露面、互動、被看見，用戶就能感受到背後是一群活生生的人，而不是一套冷冰冰的客服流程

這正好呼應了近一兩年加密圈熱議的「個人 IP」現象：當產品同質化嚴重、CEX 之間的功能差異越來越小，能真正建立差異化的，反而是團隊成員的個人品牌與信任資產

謝家印本人就是這套邏輯的活案例，他從加入 Bitget 至今，靠著高頻率的社群發文與近乎秒回的互動風格，把 Bitget 在華語市場的形象從外界眼中的「小交易所」，推進到如今用戶破億、月均交易量達數千億美元的華語前段班位置！

text:
Switched almost all our AI development workflows to GPT 6 Astra last night. We’d been running on Grok 4.6 for the last couple of weeks.  Seems much faster than Sol 5.6 so far.  My ranking for our workflow right now: Astra > Grok 4.6 > Sol 5.6.

Still early, just my experience.  Had it audit our codebases and agent skills. Plenty of things that could be improved. Now I want to see which changes actually help.  We’re a small business. Development speed matters, and I don’t want every improvement turning into a bigger project.

This is the audit prompt I’m using:  "Go through this app and look for things that make it slower to use or harder to maintain.  Start by understanding what we need it to do. Find unnecessary code, layers that add little value, and tests that don’t protect meaningful behavior. Keep the tests and safeguards that do.  Explain what’s worth changing and why, then make small, reversible changes. Don’t introduce a new framework when removing something would solve the problem.  Check the actual user flows. Measure performance before and after. If you can’t verify a change, tell me what tools or access you’re missing.  We need to move quickly and keep things safe. Keep the solution proportionate to a small business.  Leave good code alone. Don’t deploy to production."

author: RobertSagurton
quoted_text:
Most perps still work the same way.

You hit market.  
The book gets eaten level by level.  
Whoever showed up first gets the clean price.  
Everyone else gets what is left.

That is a CLOB. The queue is the product.

I sent 3 BTC on Superluminal.

The order did not walk the book.  
It got sliced into a bunch of fills.  
Every one printed $81,515.

Then I did it again with 5 BTC. Same shape.

That is DFBA. The venue waits a tiny window and clears the batch at one price. You are not boxed out because somebody clicked 3ms earlier.

Same screen. Same buy button. Different rule.

CLOB sells you a race.
DFBA just prints the price.

The ARB investor/teammate unlocks are nearing completion and will be fully unlocked this coming March. The remaining locked tokens investor/teammate account for about 7.7% of the total supply.

quoted_text:
67% of $ARB’s 10B total supply is already circulating.

That’s a high-float token.

A large portion of the eventual supply is already in the market, which means there’s less future dilution and less of the constant “unlock overhang” you typically see with low-float tokens.

So for me, fading $ARB purely because of its tokenomics doesn’t make much sense.

The supply is largely out.

Now the real question is: does demand catch up?

And this is where my $ODYS thesis gets interesting.

Robinhood Chain is built on Arbitrum, and 10% of its revenue goes back to the Arbitrum ecosystem.

Of that 10%, 2% goes specifically toward developers contributing to Arbitrum’s technology, tooling and infrastructure.

As more activity flows through Robinhood Chain and the broader Arbitrum ecosystem grows, I expect more capital to flow toward the builders and protocols contributing to that growth.

That’s why I’m betting on $ODYS.

The bet isn't just on another protocol.

It's on the ecosystem around Arbitrum getting bigger and the value that can accrue to the projects building within it.

美国中期选举，华尔街已经开始下注：小摩直接给出了三张交易地图！

离 11 月中期选举还有两个月，摩根大通已经把不同结果对应的资产赢家和输家列出来了。

医疗、军工、金融、能源、Crypto，几乎可以直接拿来当“美国政治温度计”。

现在博彩市场给出的最大概率，反而是民主党拿下参众两院，约 47%。

如果真发生，财政刺激会更偏底层消费和医疗保障，WMT、DG 这类低价零售以及医疗板块受益。代价就是监管重新变严，金融、油气、新型国防科技以及 COIN、HOOD、MSTR 这条 Crypto 线都会被压。

第二种是民主党拿众议院、共和党守参议院，概率约 39%。

这其实是华尔街最熟悉的什么都干不成：大政策互相卡住，传统军工预算反而最稳，LMT、GD、RTX 这种老军工受益，医疗继续偏利好，但投行和资本市场业务缺乏进一步放松监管的催化。

真正值得 Crypto 圈记住的是第三种：

共和党继续控制参众两院，目前只有约 16% 概率。

这个结果一旦开始被市场重新定价，交易的就不只是特朗普概念，而是整个放松监管组合——GS、MS 等金融，油气管道、原材料、美国制造业回流、新型军工，以及 COIN、HOOD、MSTR 都会同时受益。

Crypto 还有一层独立催化：国会结构越偏共和党，类似 CLARITY Act 这类加密市场结构立法继续推进的阻力越小。

所以接下来两个月，中期选举直接会影响市场的走势，一定要盯紧。

如果共和党两院胜率开始持续往上爬，Crypto、金融、能源和国防科技很可能会比大盘更早告诉你：

钱已经开始押选举了。

text:
Gyndore GLB TL;DR ⤵

The easiest way to understand Gyndore’s Liquidity Bootstrapping Event: It’s not just selling $GYND. It’s using the sale to fund liquidity that the protocol itself owns.

The GLB opens 15 September at 3PM UTC.

- 2M GYND for sale = 20% of the fixed 10M supply
- Price: $0.10
- Starting FDV: $1M
- Maximum raise: $200K
- Max purchase: 100K GYND / $10K per wallet
- Runs for 48 hours or until sold out

If fully subscribed, roughly:

$200K raised
→ 50% funds the GYND/cbBTC launch market on @HydrexFi
→ 50% funds cbBTC, USDC, USDT and ETH trading liquidity

So instead of raising money primarily for operations, Gyndore converts the capital into protocol-owned liquidity.

GYND stakers receive 100% of protocol revenue in USDC, distributed continuously, with no staking lockup.

The twist is that, If the 2M GYND allocation doesn't sell out, the unsold tokens are distributed to buyers as bGYND bonuses.

bGYND:

- Is backed 1:1 by GYND
- Earns the same staking rewards
- Has no official liquid market
- Can eventually be converted into GYND by paying 70% of GYND's market price

That effectively gives holders a 30% conversion discount, assuming GYND trades at or above $0.10.

Pretty interesting LBP, if I may say, especially considering that @base is pushing their chain with more utility projects like Gyndore.

Less noise, more Sats.

text:
In 2021 people sold Charizards to ape into NFTs

In 2025 they sold Bitcoin to buy Charizards

Same wallets
Same rotation
Different year

2020 and 2021 lit both markets at once. Stimulus, lockdowns, the 25th anniversary, and the Bitcoin bull run sent card prices parabolic. Then late 2021 attention flipped to crypto and NFTs. Cardboard cooled. 2022 wrecked both. Cards dumped. Bitcoin fell about 75%.
2024 started the loop again. ETFs and the halving revived crypto. Money flowed back into Pokémon through new sets, TCG Pocket, and 151 nostalgia. By 2025 Bitcoin tagged around $126k while high end cases were getting paid in BTC and ETH. Then 2026 flipped the scoreboard. Bitcoin corrected hard. Cards kept winning on the year

Now it is September 2026 and the 30th anniversary set drops on the 16th. That is the current TCG heat candle, the same job the 25th did last cycle.
Why it keeps repeating: millennials who ripped packs as kids are the same people who bought Bitcoin. Gains in one become bids in the other

Both run on scarcity, nostalgia, and FOMO, not cash flow. They often pump together. The rotation shows up at the peaks

That is why people are saying the Pokémon cycle is topping and crypto is next. Not advice. Just the rhyme.

text:
这轮牛市里，波动率溢价还会集中在短期限的期权里吗？

看到Lucic和Sepp之前关于加密期权的一篇研究

他们用 2019 到 2023 年 Deribit的BTC、ETH期权数据，对不同期限和期权组合进行回测，同时把Delta Hedge、Funding、再平衡和交易成本都算进去，尽量剥离方向影响，观察波动率本身能留下的收益

结果是，经过Delta 对冲以后，多种卖波动策略依然能够保持正收益，而且期限越短，这种波动率风险溢价越明显

像BTC Short Straddle（DDH）

1W年化 32.5%；1M年化 12.6%；3M年化 8.5%

周度的25Delta Short Strangle年化也达到了 22.2%，Sharpe 0.99

收益不仅呈现出直观的梯度，其中短期限期权的风险溢价也更显著，BTC上的表现又比 ETH 更明显

看了这篇研究，我现在倒是好奇，这轮牛市里持续卖短期限的波动，最后会是什么结果？@JeffLia12309881

text:
Everyone should be able to access high-quality financial assets, wherever they live.

That's what tokenization unlocks: taking the best of US capital markets and making them available on a global scale.

The industry is still small compared with global finance, but the advantages are becoming harder to ignore. Traditional market infrastructure was built around fixed hours, closed networks and layers of intermediaries. It was never designed for 24/7 execution, programmable assets, composability or self-custody.

The needs of investors have moved faster than the rails underneath them. We're working to change that.

What gives me confidence is seeing how many different people are now pushing this industry forward. Founders are building new products, LPs are bringing liquidity, traders are finding new uses, and infrastructure teams are making the whole thing work.

It's a privilege to be in the trenches with all of you.

We are still early, and there is a huge amount left to build. It will also take time and effort for the old guard to get onboard. This is worth fighting for.

text:
the quoted post is an understandable but very implausible counterfactual

once a couple teams showed you don't go to jail if:
-->you run a very centralized chain with just a handful of permissioned validators
-->you run a very centralized chain with one validator and call it an "L2"

the cat was out of the bag 

the proliferation of many centralized chains whose operators capture almost all of the value from them was inevitable, rather than the Robinhoods of the world merely being apps on Ethereum or Solana 

the difference is that Ethereum provided a convenient way for these chains to at least still be somewhat connected to Ethereum, save some money by being single-operator, and potentially use ETH as money

not pretending this was some brilliant strategy on Ethereum's part--the intent was to "scale Ethereum" but we accidentally created a weird and somewhat illogical regulatory arb for centralized operators instead

but it works, and is more beneficial to Ethereum/ETH than them just being separate "appchains"

Here are a few independently verified figures about the frontline dynamics, showing that Russia is not winning and will not win this war:

- According to open sources, the net balance between areas occupied by Russia and those liberated by Ukraine in August 2026 was roughly +5 square kilometers. While the figure is approximate, the trend is clear. Meanwhile, Moscow lost at least 42,000 troops killed and wounded—one of its highest monthly casualty rates of the war.

- Open-source data shows that in August 2026 alone, in response to Russian attacks, there were a record 70 successful Ukrainian long-range sanctions against legitimate military targets in Russia (5 more than in July).

- Over the first eight months of 2026, the average pace of Russia’s already slow advance was 3.5 times slower than in 2025. Russia has occupied less than 0.2% of additional Ukrainian territory this year.

- Even in the Donbas, where Russian forces concentrate most of their effort, Russia has failed to achieve an operational breakthrough and still does not control 20% of the Donetsk region. At its current pace, it would take the Russian occupiers over two years to capture that remaining land.

Whatever fabricated maps Russian generals present to Putin, the reality on the ground shows that he is not winning and will not win this war. 

Given the situation in the Russian economy and its inability to counter Ukraine’s long-range sanctions, things will only get worse for Russia.

Yes, it’s very difficult for Ukraine as well. For our warriors, frontline communities, and all of our country. We are in the fifth year of full-scale war that we didn’t choose. Every family has been scarred by it in one way or another.

But clearly, Moscow is not in a strong position either. And certainly not in a position to dictate terms.

text:
Took a few days away this last week and of course it had to coincide with the mania happening on Robinhood’s flagship Ethereum L2 🙈

I spent too much time staring at @fomo (@Markets_xyz also deserves attention too but only supports HL trading so no RH tokens). 

You will regret not downloading these apps to simply check out how seamless mobile trading can be. The next bull run happens here—trading more on mobile vs what some of us experienced with desktop browser apps for DeFi and CEXs.

I’ve also seen posts like @sjdedic’s hypothesizing “no one’s actually making money” and although I understand his point, one I made about Pump, my pushback is that i) fewer are realizing profits this early on RH and ii) the numbers likely reflect how few have the skill set to trade profitably, especially with only market swaps, in a world dominated by cabal insider trading (see what Frankdegods did with MEME 🤡).

My experience over just a few weeks was many tokens were running, it felt hard to keep up, but specifically those promoted by the biggest traders on Fomo run the hardest, and it is still hard to pick out runners without the endorsement of some CT trading god first. Basically anyone can buy/sell on the major L1s/L2s with Fomo but most are focused on micro-cap memecoins endorsed by big trading accounts.

Feels almost like 2017 all over again where everyone’s buying the same tokens. This time though you can see realtime trades from anyone you follow and get alerts, leading to super reflexive price action on small cap tokens that can run from sub-$1M to sometimes $100 to $200 million market caps. Totally ridiculous and it is a moment we are living through.

There is very little liq to sell into on RH tokens, most of the biggest holders have prisoners dilemma unless they’re outright crooks who farm and dump on their following but I have seen a lot more holding unrealized gains among the biggest accounts, in a few weeks.

It is too early to tell which RH tokens might be legit value accruing tokens to rise from this froth other than a few ($PONS) or clever memes tied to tokenized stocks (ie BONER = HIMS or AI = NVDA). There’s a whole meta playing out with memecoins tied to stocks and forcing some interesting arb dynamics between tokenized stocks on RH vs the real equities.

Is there cabal insider trading? Yes
Is liquidity laughably thin? Of course 
Are many failing to take profits? Yup
Will some roundtrip back to 0? Probably

But “is everyone losing?” Idk, it looks more normal to me than the Pump mania last cycle, or TRUMP/MELANIA trading where at least now we can see some real time trades from big holders (even though I’m sure some are selling in undisclosed wallets). 

Best takeaway is RH Chain is proving what mega-fintechs can do to launch as their own Ethereum L2 and be a landlord vs a tenant of an alt-L1. 

🔗 https://t.co/tPHshoq554

Note: I am holding PONS, I have been trading it a short time, wish I just bought and simply held, but I could sell again if it’s grossly overvalued, don’t follow me on fomo for long term investing—I am public about what I long but private about the value of those holdings over years and my Fomo/Markets accounts will be for trading.

text:
Tether-Backed Chilean Crypto Exchange Orionx Shuts Down After $7M+ Asset Shortfall  

Chilean crypto exchange Orionx has begun a permanent shutdown after a forensic audit found that more than $7 million in customer assets had been transferred to wallets outside the company’s control. Withdrawals are suspended, and Orionx has filed criminal complaints against co-founders Roberto Zibert and Joaquín Díaz over alleged transfers of BTC, ETH, XRP and POL between 2018 and 2021; both deny wrongdoing.   

Chile’s financial regulator rejected Orionx’s registration application in June 2026. Tether invested in Orionx in June 2025, exclusively leading its Series A round, though the original announcement is no longer available on Tether’s website.

quoted_text:
Offchain Labs and Solana Co-Founders Debate Robinhood Chain Fee Model

Offchain Labs co-founder Steven Goldfeder and Solana co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko debated Robinhood Chain’s fee model. Yakovenko said the 10% revenue share paid to Arbitrum would have been enough to cover Solana transaction fees four times over, allowing Robinhood to offer users a fully gasless experience.

Goldfeder called that a “ridiculous take,” saying Robinhood keeps about 90% of gas fees on Arbitrum, whereas on Solana it would retain none of the base-layer fees and would have to subsidize user fees out of pocket. “Robinhood chose Arbitrum so they could be a landlord and not a tenant,” he wrote.

Yakovenko argued that Robinhood could charge users at the frontend while lowering costs by using a cheaper backend. Goldfeder replied that most of the fees are generated by activity that does not pass through Robinhood’s frontend. If Robinhood were merely a tenant on another chain, he said, it would capture none of that ancillary activity, even if it had brought those users there.

Everyone should be able to access high-quality financial assets, wherever they live.

That's what tokenization unlocks: taking the best of US capital markets and making them available on a global scale.

The industry is still small compared with global finance, but the advantages are becoming harder to ignore. Traditional market infrastructure was built around fixed hours, closed networks and layers of intermediaries. It was never designed for 24/7 execution, programmable assets, composability or self-custody.

The needs of investors have moved faster than the rails underneath them. We're working to change that.

What gives me confidence is seeing how many different people are now pushing this industry forward. Founders are building new products, LPs are bringing liquidity, traders are finding new uses, and infrastructure teams are making the whole thing work.

It's a privilege to be in the trenches with all of you.

We are still early, and there is a huge amount left to build. It will also take time and effort for the old guard to get onboard. This is worth fighting for.

@StockYieldMoney = an onchain capital markets layer built around tokenized stocks.

text:
我这两天一直在想一个挺让人不舒服的问题。

我们在社交媒体上反复看到的那些「AI 要让你失业」「AI 会取代绝大多数人」「人类很快就没用了」的叙事，到底有多少是真实判断，又有多少是有人花钱买出来的？

Sabine Hossenfelder 最近说，她收到过付费邀约，希望她去传播对 AI 的恐惧。

Wes Roth 转述得更激进一点，有些钱甚至会被包装成 grant，也就是「资助」，所以观众可能根本不知道，这些看起来像独立观点的内容，背后其实存在利益关系。

这件事目前最关键的证据链，我觉得还不能说完全坐实。Sabine 确实公开说过有人愿意付钱让创作者讲 AI 会杀死我们，也提到 AI 乐观派和悲观派两边都存在出钱影响内容的情况。

但具体是谁出了钱、哪些创作者拿过钱、有没有明确要求隐瞒赞助，目前公开证据还不够。

但这已经足够让我重新看待过去一两年互联网上的 AI 叙事。

我跟我老婆聊过很多次 AI 会不会取代人的问题。我的判断一直没那么悲观，我觉得现实里的工作远比 benchmark 和 demo 复杂，AI 能把很多环节做掉，不等于一家公司从此不需要人。

但她有时候会更焦虑。原因也很简单，每隔一阵就会有一个新模型出来，然后整个社交媒体开始刷屏，程序员要没了，设计师要没了，白领要没了，这次是真的 AGI 了。再配上一堆很夸张的 demo，很容易让一个不天天研究 AI 的人形成一种感觉，是不是再过两年，所有事情机器都能做了。

后来我才意识到，很多普通人对 AI 的认识，本来就不是来自论文、产品使用或者真实工作场景。

他们认识 AI 的方式，就是信息流。

而信息流最喜欢的东西，恰好是恐慌。

如果背后再叠加一层资本和机构利益，这件事就更值得警惕了。

因为「AI 很危险」本身也是一种非常值钱的叙事。

它可以让一家公司的技术显得更强，让一个研究机构的重要性变高，让监管议题获得更多预算，也可以让某些投资标的继续维持这是一场决定人类未来的技术革命的估值想象。

所以以后看到 AI 马上取代所有人这种内容，我会多问一句这个观点是谁在说，谁在为它买单，以及谁会因为所有人相信它而获利。

这当然不意味着 AI 风险是假的，也不意味着 AI 不会冲击就业。真正的问题是，我们现在正在用一种很糟糕的方式，让社会接受这项技术。

过去两年，科技行业太喜欢用恐慌教育用户了。这些话传播起来很快，也确实能让更多人冲进去用产品。

但我觉得，一个真正重要的新技术，不应该靠吓人来完成普及。

媒体和科技公司应该做的，是告诉大家它现在到底能做什么、做不到什么，哪些工作会改变，哪些能力会变得更重要。让人理解这个东西，再决定怎么跟它相处。

最近校园招聘，很多同学问我：现在AI这么强，应届校招生还有机会吗？
前两天黄仁勋在GTC大会说了段话，挺有意思的，我挺想跟大家聊聊。
他说AI不会让人没工作，反而会让人越来越忙。过去一个月的工作量，现在30分钟就能完成。
AI把“做完”的门槛拉得特别低了，但“做好”这件事，依然需要人的判断力。
我觉得AI能做出什么，取决于手里有什么材料，以及大家对这些材料的判断力。AI可以帮大家执行，但它不知道什么是好的、什么方向是对的。这些东西，只能靠大家在真实世界里一点点攒出来。
真实世界的经验和判断力，AI替代不了。
在美团我从实习开始，销售、商分、产品都做过。后来创业做水滴，最底层的判断力，都是那几年攒出来的。
水滴每年也都有很多校招生的HC。这个时代依然需要人的成长、人的温度、人的判断，这些东西AI或许很难学会。

text:
Price tells you what already happened. Options flow tells you where money is being committed Right now

That gap is why TreyBae exists

I'm the sole developer. Almost seven years in the markets, no team, no funding. Here's the thing about the other flow platforms: they charge $50+/mo like they've got pricing power. They don't. It's the same feed on every dashboard — cluttered, hard to read, and expensive before you can even tell if the tool fits how you trade. The feed isn't the edge. How you read it is. So I built the reader I actually wanted.

The bubble map is the heart of it. Every bubble is a stock, and it answers two questions most platforms blur into one: which side is the money on — calls or puts — and who was the aggressor — were those contracts being bought or sold. That second axis matters. A stock can be 76% calls while every one of those calls is being SOLD. That's a bearish position built out of call contracts, and a one-axis view calls it bullish every time.

Size tells you how strange today's volume is against open interest. Color tells you how hard the lean. A slow pulse means money is arriving fast, right now. The whole market's positioning, one screen.

Double-click any bubble for the full workup — the chain with a lean meter on every expiry, insider filings (grants don't count as buys here), institutional holders, IV, P/E history, and the large prints themselves.

Then there's the Sonar. It only draws a name when three independent measurements agree — lean, pressure, unusual volume — counted as votes, never blended into a score. Most of the day it's nearly empty. That's on purpose. A screen where everything lights up is a screen where nothing does.

Gold on the Sonar is a verified whale: a single $250K+ trade, filled at the ask, today, on the side the name is already leaning. All four required. It almost never fires. That's exactly why it means something when it does.

And the terminal is free. Not a trial — the full board, no card. A free account adds Time Machine: rewind the entire board hour by hour and watch positioning build instead of only seeing where it ended up.

Two tiers sit on top:

Supporter ($4.99) — unlimited lookups, saved pins and layouts.

Pro ($14.99) — Quant Signals: rules-based entries, targets, and time windows, fired automatically. A starting point for your own research, not a verdict.

House rules, because this market runs on unlabeled numbers: every stat on the site says whether it's backtested or live. Performance is published, misses included. Weak signals are flagged as weak. If you find a number that doesn't say how it was measured, that's a bug —  lmk

I work on this seven days a week. This is my life's work.

TreyBae is an informational and educational tool. It shows you what's happening in the options market; it doesn't tell you what to trade. Nothing on the site is investment advice, I'm not a registered investment adviser, and trading carries substantial risk of loss. Always do your own research.

text:
Everyone is talking about what AI agents will be able to do.

- Book flights.
- Manage funds. 
- Write code. 
- Make purchases. 
- Negotiate. 
- Make decisions for us.

But there’s a question we’re going to have to answer eventually:

Who takes responsibility when an AI agent gets it wrong?

A human employee can be held accountable. A company operates within a legal framework.

But an autonomous agent?

You can’t simply point at OpenAI or Anthropic every time an agent makes a bad decision.

And the more economic responsibility we hand over to agents, the bigger this problem becomes.

That’s why this part of the @GenLayer Agent Tank livestream hits like crack!

The idea of insurance for AI agents was talked about , where disputes around an agent’s actions could be judged to determine what actually went wrong and who should be compensated.

I think this is where AI infrastructure starts getting really interesting.

We spend so much time building agents that can act autonomously.

Now we need infrastructure that can hold those actions accountable.

Because an agentic economy can’t scale on autonomy alone.

It also needs trust.

The Lmax_v11 framework is built from a single geometric insight about the electromagnetic spectrum: EM waves may reach arbitrarily high frequencies, but they cannot propagate indefinitely across distance. The spectrum is immortal in proper time — photons experience zero time between emission and absorption — yet not immortal in space. Because a photon’s worldline is null, all internal evolution must occur along distance, not time. As the EM field stretches across the affine parameter, its oscillatory structure weakens, wavelength dilates, amplitude decreases, and the noise‑frequency threshold approaches. This geometric evolution cannot continue forever. It must reach a final state.

Lmaxv11 shows that the EM field has a finite geometric lifespan: a maximum affine distance \(L{\max}\). This limit appears consistently across the observational record — the pristine 76.125 Gly ceiling, the 76 Gly void limit, the 68–72 Gly dense‑region limits, and the 45.56 Gly CMB corridor shaped by gravitational tension. The EM field exists only while oscillation remains above the universal noise floor. When the stretched geometry reaches \(L_{\max}\), oscillation becomes unsustainable and collapse occurs. The photon does not enter a “dead zone”; it ceases at the boundary. Energy does not vanish. It transitions into matter in high‑tension environments or into non‑oscillatory geometric residue (QGR) in low‑tension environments.

This framework does not claim proof and is not peer‑reviewed. It shows a coherent geometric reinterpretation of existing data: redshift, flux dimming, horizon structure, and CMB placement arise from geometric stretch and gravitational modulation of the affine limit rather than from metric expansion. The EM spectrum has no known upper frequency bound — the highest observed photons reach ~10³⁴ Hz — but it does exhibit a finite propagation boundary. In this view, the electromagnetic field is immortal in proper time but mortal in distance, with \(L_{\max}\) defining the geometric horizon of oscillatory existence.

text:
为何中国财政部集中向国有金融机构注资、发生了什么？也不要大惊小怪，去年（2025年）财政部也集中向一批国有大型商业银行注资，而且方式和今年非常类似。
1）2025年3月30日，中国银行、建设银行、交通银行、邮储银行四家国有大行同日发布向特定对象发行A股股票预案，合计拟募集资金约5200亿元，全部用于补充核心一级资本。其中财政部认购5000亿元，资金来源正是当年发行的5000亿元“中央金融机构注资特别国债”。另外还有中国烟草、中国移动、中国船舶等央企参与部分认购。
这笔资金在2025年6月下旬全部到账，四家银行定增落地。

这是财政部时隔20多年再次通过特别国债大规模注资国有大行，也25年初政府工作报告里提到的是“统筹推进、分期分批、一行一策”安排中的第一批。

2）今年（2026年）9月6日的动作，本质上是同一轮政策的延续和第二批落地：覆盖此前尚未注资的工商银行、农业银行，并首次把保险机构和政策性金融机构纳入，规模从去年的5000亿元调整为3000亿元特别国债支持。

两轮注资的核心逻辑一致：
1）都是前瞻性补充核心一级资本，国有大行作为全球系统重要性银行，面临更高资本缓冲和TLAC要求，部分机构分组上调后标准将进一步收紧；

2）息差持续收窄导致内源资本积累放缓，房地产和地方债务等领域仍有潜在压力。外部注资能迅速增厚“安全垫”，提升抗风险能力，属于“未雨绸缪”而非应急输血；增强风险抵御能力；

3）资本具有乘数效应，1元核心资本可撬动数倍信贷。两轮注资释放数万亿元贷款空间，定向支持科技创新、绿色转型、基建、“三农”和出口，服务实体经济的信贷投放空间。​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

4）2026年进一步覆盖保险机构，也是因为国债收益率持续下行，导致保险机构准备金增提，净资产承压，核心偿付能力指标面临下行风险。注资保险机构既夯实偿付能力，也释放险资作为耐心资本入市；政策性机构则强化对外开放职能。

整体是积极财政政策与金融政策协同，在经营指标总体健康的前提下，主动增强金融体系韧性和服务实体经济的持续能力。

有两个思考点：
1）宣布注资时机
25-26年第一批宣布向国有金融机构注册是25年3月30日，正好是川普关税战的最关键时刻（4月2日是“解放日”）；
今年第二批注册宣布时间正值中方领导人访美前两周；

2）是否会有配套政策出台
其实梳理下历史上98年、03-08年、10年后、25年3月最近注资的第一批。历次注资都不是孤立行动，后续往往伴随降息降准、增发国债等一系列宽松政策……

今天集中宣布的新一批向国有金融机构注资，会不会再有新的配套政策出来？如果有，放出来的水是否会定向涌向AI等新质生产力领域？更值得思考🤔

text:
今天套利周会也专门复盘了这件事。

1. 这个事情大概是什么

他在 Binance 做资金费率套利，账户里有 30 多个套利仓位。北京时间 9 月 3 日凌晨 5:44，这些仓位被集中强平，单日损失超过 500 万 USDT，本金几乎归零。典型的资金费率套利，是买入现货，同时做空永续合约，用现货的上涨抵消空单的亏损，再赚空头收到的资金费。但 Delta 中性只解决价格方向问题，不会自动解决保证金、流动性和强平问题。

2. 当时发生了什么

AKE 从 9 月 2 日晚上 9 点左右的 0.0076，一直涨到 9 月 3 日凌晨 5:44 的 0.044859，8 个多小时接近 6 倍。最剧烈的一段发生在 5:37 到 5:44，价格从 0.022432 涨到 0.044859，7 分钟翻倍。

资金费率是慢慢赚的，强平却可能在几分钟内发生。如果空单使用杠杆，或者多个仓位共享同一个保证金账户，AKE 的快速上涨会让空头保证金迅速下降。即使另一边持有现货，现货浮盈也不一定能实时转到合约账户补保证金。30 多个仓位看起来很分散，但如果都是做空低流动性、高资金费的小币，本质上还是同一个风险。一个币发生极端逼空，就可能把整个账户的仓位一起带走。

3. Binance 应不应该承担损失

我目前倾向于 Binance 不应该直接承担这次交易损失，但前提是它公开说的价格源和清算机制确实正常。

Binance 的回复是，当时 AKE 的上涨同时发生在多个主流平台和链上，并不是 Binance 单个平台突然插针。Binance 本身也没有 AKE 现货，AKEUSDT 永续合约参考的是外部现货市场的指数价格，强平主要使用 mark price，而不是 Binance 合约市场某一笔最新成交价。

这里需要纠正一个说法。不是“所有 CEX 都有问题”，而是多个 CEX 和链上现货同时上涨。如果 Binance 的指数、mark price 和强平日志都符合公开规则，这更接近全市场价格变化带来的正常合约风险，不能因为亏损很大，就直接要求平台赔偿。

这和 8 月 9 日的 TUT 事件有一个关键区别。TUT 当时出现了明显的交易所价格分叉：公开复盘中，Binance 价格最高约 0.3056，Gate 一度到约 0.70，Bitget 的标记价格最高接近 1.006。Bitget 后来承认存在标记价格异常和流动性失衡，并对异常时段受影响的用户提出赔付方案。

所以 TUT 的赔付逻辑是“某个平台的价格和清算系统明显偏离其他市场”；AKE 目前看到的情况，则是链上现货和多个交易市场一起上涨。发帖者提到的 TUT 先例，更接近 Bitget 对自身价格异常的处理，并不能直接推出 Binance 也应该为 AKE 赔偿。

当然，如果后续日志证明 Binance 的指数成分、mark price、强平时间或订单执行出现异常，那责任判断需要重新做。

4. 套利者可以怎么应对

群友给出一个经验，是持续监控价格涨幅。标的相对开仓价上涨到一定程度后，先主动减仓，等价格、基差和流动性稳定，再逐步加回来。这样降低爆仓成单腿的风险。

如果原来做的是现货多、永续空，减仓时最好按对冲比例同时缩小两条腿。这样可以释放保证金、拉远强平价，同时避免减完空单以后，组合突然变成方向性多头。

除此之外，还应该有更硬的保护：

- 每个小币设置独立风险预算，不能让一个币吃掉整个账户；
- 尽量使用逐仓，不让一笔异常行情传染到其他仓位；
- 同时监控价格加速度、基差、盘口深度、强平距离、资金费率和指数价格；
- 预先计算真实可退出规模，不能只看屏幕上的价差；
- 数据异常、盘口消失或者价格快速拉升时，程序自动降仓或停机；
- 资金费再高，也不能覆盖没有上限的尾部风险。

如果判断市场正在发生逼空，也可以设计反向跟随、高位做空或者其他异常行情策略。但这些已经是方向性交易或事件交易，需要单独的资金、仓位和止损，不能再把它叫作无风险套利。

5. 庄家可能怎么从这种行情里赚钱

下面只能算一种可能的操盘机制，目前没有证据证明 AKE 一定是这样完成的。

小市值合约币的现货流动性很薄，筹码也可能集中。操盘者可以先观察合约市场的持仓量、资金费率和空头集中程度。如果市场上已经堆积了大量套利空单或投机空单，他可以提前在永续合约建立多头，再去链上或其他现货市场持续买入，把现货价格推高。

因为 CEX 的永续指数和 mark price 通常会参考外部现货价格，现货上涨会逐步传导到合约。空头接近强平线后，系统强平会产生被动买单，这些买单又会继续推高合约价格，形成“现货拉升 → mark price 上涨 → 空头强平 → 合约继续上涨”的链条。

操盘者可以在强平买盘出现时平掉提前埋伏的合约多单，也可以把低位买入的现货卖给追涨资金。等空头和追涨盘被清理以后，再反向交易价格回落。

这种收割看起来很有确定性，是因为大额空头的强平位置具有一定可预测性。但它并不真正确定：拉现货需要成本，指数价格通常有多个来源和保护机制，其他套利者也可能反向交易，操盘者同样可能被套。链上转账、筹码集中和价格上涨能提供怀疑线索，但还不足以证明具体主体和操纵意图。

有点黑暗森林的感觉，感谢大哥 500WU 给大家交了个学费🫡

quoted_text:
AI is the best thing to ever happen to $BTC and $ETH, and we are about to watch it all unfold, here is why:

As technology becomes more political, neutral technology becomes more valuable.

AI has changed the risk profile of technology investing in an incredibly short amount of time. So much so that today, in the big ‘26, memory businesses cannot even be called businesses so much as strategic assets caught in the middle of a technological arms race between two increasingly uncertain superpowers. 

AKA: The better Chinese AI tech gets, the more investors have to price geopolitical uncertainty into U.S. AI infrastructure. The better the U.S. responds, the more Chinese assets end up facing the same problem.

This is where Bitcoin and Ethereum become interesting as two highly liquid, geographically distributed, immutable assets that no single company issues and no single government controls.

TLDR: They are the ONLY major assets structurally incapable of being pulled into the wars to come.

“But wait..what about macro.”

Historically, this is fair, because BTC and ETH have traded like high beta tech since the marginal buyer was a speculator borrowing against a calm world.

But in case you have not noticed, we are not in a calm world anymore. 

Let’s break it down:

A tech equity is a claim on cash flows, and cash flows are now hostage to policy, example: 

- Export licenses now set Nvidia’s addressable market. 
- Subsidy regimes are what decide where the fabs rise. 
- a single directive can immediately reroute a supply chain. 

Essentially, the better centralized technology gets, the more strategic it becomes and the more strategic it becomes, the less it belongs to its shareholders and the more it belongs to national interests.

Bitcoin and Ethereum on the other hand, are built different (literally), they are truly sovereign, and highly liquid. Every escalation elsewhere that adds risk premium to strategic tech adds monetary premium to that sovereignty.

As people grok this,  the marginal buyer is likely to shift from a speculator chasing tech beta to an allocator effectively purchasing insurance against the political capture of technology.

We will look back on this AI race as the moment the world changed its mind about BTC and ETH, where for the very first time,  “volatile tech” changed its mask and became “sanctuary tech.“

A store of value for an era when value itself became a weapon.

A return to Satoshi’s promise.

text:
Few people understand the improbability of Lindsay Clancy having psychosis at 8 months postpartum and that leading to her killing her children, so let me quantify using the available data:
1. Incidence of postpartum psychosis: ~0.15%
2. Homicide in untreated first-episode psychosis: ~0.16%
3. Postpartum disease peaks between 10-19 days.
4. The data on incidence of postpartum psychosis cited above stops at 3 months because most literature agrees that beyond that it asymptotically approaches 0. 

Conditional probability that she had PPP and killed her children from it = 0.0000024 or 1/416,667. BUT that’s at 3 months. At 8 months? I’ll go on a limb and say probably 0.

However, people try to suggest that because Remeron has the very rare side effect of psychosis so it must’ve been drug-induced. Ok, she was also on Seroquel which is an antipsychotic. I guess that simpleton argument is neutralized. 

Because anything is possible, you have to analyze the incident in real time. When you do, you realize it’s absolutely silly to suggest that she hopped into psychosis for 18 minutes, murdered her children, then just hopped right back out without intervention.
author: Selkis_2028
quoted_text:
I avoided commenting on the Lindsay Clancy trial because its nuanced and emotional but the implications are enormous so I am going to say something now. A lot of people are calling that one juror who wouldn't join the other eleven irrational. But, that juror is probably the only one asking the right questions imo: where is the evidence that she lacked the capacity to know it was wrong or to stop herself? And, maybe, where do we draw the line on what an ostensibly insane person is allowed to do when the doubt the defense manufactured rests on nothing in the record before the killings? It seems that the entirety of the defense position rests on improbable probabilities and that's a low bar for such a heinous act.

1. Postpartum psychosis is rare, and almost always happens in the first 4 weeks. The idea that some psychiatrists extend the postpartum window to a year is true, but for depression and anxiety. The evidence isn't strong for psychosis, and its latching on to improbability

2. The strongest risk factor for postpartum psychosis is preexisting bipolar disorder or a prior psychotic episode. She had neither before her third child. The real time evidence from her doctors/providers indicate this. The bipolar label that showed up was after significant polypharmacy, and any good psychiatrist will tell you that you cannot diagnose primary disease when multiple drugs could be offending agents. Drug-induced psychosis would show better temporal correlations with her medications and should be a mitigation argument at sentencing. Again, very improbable alignment

3. The proxy for intent is planning, and she clearly planned... she sent her husband to some restaurant they don't normally go to, checked the drive time, texted a specific order at 5:07 pm... she killed her children in sequence. That's demonstrating real time decision making. I don't understand how they circumvented this. Again, very improbable that she was able to make decisions up until it becomes a liability

4. This idea of a "voice" that commanded her is so post-hoc as a defense. The ltierature on command hallucinations show most people don't obey them and the compliance occurs when the voice is familiar. This was a first time voice she only ever reported 2 weeks after killing her kids. And this first time voice asked her to... kill all her children AND she listened to this unfamiliar voice? Again... very improbable

The improbability is so stark that it's almost undeniably a sympathy verdict from the jurors conflated with a misunderstanding of postpartum disease. The easiest way to demonstrate this is to take a father with the same chart, months of documented depression, insomnia, suicidal ideation but no psychosis then strangles his kids after arranging for his wife to be away from the house. 100% guilty.

Everyone knows postpartum disease is real and important. Everyone knows she's sick and needed help, possibly much better management. You can even argue she is insane. What I see to be the most important is where we draw the line of what we allow under the "insanity" rule. Massachusetts forces a binary verdict of guilty or not criminally responsible but this is a case for the third that other states have and which is guilty but mentally ill. We have a responsibility to speak for the unheard voices of these children and future children and say we draw the line at murdering children.
