text:
If you are new to $STONK

Here is probably the easiest way to understand the entire ecosystem from zero:

STONK is basically a meme token on Solana built around the StonkFun ecosystem.

The easiest way to think about it is:

$STONK = the token
StonkFun = the launchpad/system around it

StonkFun basically combines two of the biggest speculative narratives:

Pre-IPO stocks + memecoins.

Instead of being just another isolated meme

The idea is to create an entire launch and discovery system around these assets.

The flow is basically:

- A token launches through StonkFun.
- StonkFun identifies it as part of the ecosystem.

And users can then discover and trade these assets through a more social trading experience.

StonkFun has already been integrated into Fomo App.

Meaning users can see whether a token was originally launched through StonkFun.

But there is another integration coming that makes the system much more interesting:

Launchlab.

The upcoming Launchlab integration is expected to change deployments

Add bonding curves
And improve the entire launch experience.

Now let’s understand bonding curves.

A bonding curve basically makes the token price increase as more demand enters.

More people buy
The token moves further along the curve

And the price increases.

This makes it much easier to launch and discover the price of completely new tokens.

And also heavily rewards being early.

So the entire system starts looking like this:

StonkFun launches the asset
Bonding curves create the initial price discovery

Now we get to $STONK itself.

And the token has been one of the strongest performers recently.

Over the last 30 days

STONK went from:

$0.00723

To:

$0.17897

With approximately: $225.6M in cumulative DEX volume.

So there is clearly real trading activity around the token.

So if you want to follow $STONK

There are basically three things I would watch:

- StonkFun adoption
- Fomo + Launchlab integrations
- DEX volume and large holder movements

Because if StonkFun keeps attracting launches

And the pre-IPO stock narrative keeps growing

STONK could become one of the most interesting speculative ecosystems on Solana.

Proud to back @facto_to in our @EASYResidency Season 4.

Almost every crypto card today is a prepaid card in disguise. Card networks want an answer in under a second, blockchains don't settle that fast, so issuers make you park cash in a card balance before you can spend a dollar.

Facto fixes this at the infra layer: authorize now, settle later. Tap your card, Facto checks your actual onchain balance and answers instantly, and its settlement pool fronts the payment while the chain catches up.

So your stablecoins and DeFi positions become directly spendable. No pre-funding, no top-ups. The dollars keep earning yield until the second you tap.

Longer term, every authorized transaction builds execution history: the foundation for underwriting onchain credit beyond identity-based scoring. Cards first, credit layer next.

Follow @dreambig_peter @realdora_eth on their journey of making every dollar onchain spendable.

如果你无法理解这个新闻，你就顺着钱流向解读

财政部注资给这些机构，但是财政部没有钱，而是财政部发国债募资金，这些国债谁买？
答案是也是工行和烟草公司出钱购买，于是财政部借工行的钱，去给工行注资，有人不理解了，这不是脱裤子放屁吗？
其实不然，工行里的钱不是工行的，是储户的，在财务报表上，储户的钱是工行的负债，是工行欠储户的，当财政部出面以发债的形式从工行借出时，这笔钱性质就变了，从储户和工行的债务关系，变成了储户、工行和财政部的三角债，当财政部再把钱注资回工行时，是以投资的形式进行，就像你给自己企业对公户投资一样，这成了投资行为，不是债务问题，债是要还的，投资则是面临亏损的，只有赚钱时才能拿回钱

问题是现在的工行赚钱吗？或者说还能继续赚大钱吗？去看看银行人这两年到处吐槽的降薪潮你就明白了，好吧，既然不赚钱财政部为何还要投钱？
答案是优化工行的资产和负债比，说的再具体一点就是，当工行做亏损减记时，可以用注资的钱来填窟窿，好让工行财报继续看起来稳健，比如工行一笔房贷确定收不回来时，就必须计提减损，或者把信用卡借款打一折卖给催收公司，这中的差价亏损就必须要人来填，财政部显然就是这个大冤种

工行是这样，几家保险机构也是同类，他们担保了太多风险，随着经济继续下行，这些保单也是陆续亏损，他们也要优化资产负债表，但是这个钱有部分是烟草公司来出，本质就是拿稳赚不赔的烟草公司利润，去填这些保险机构亏损

这种操作是中国经济全面恶化，债务烂账集中爆发的表现，只是在中共宣传中是不允许这样说的，他们把这包装成了跟央行降息一样的宽松利好

全世界房地产泡沫破灭时，都会有银行和保险金融机构倒闭，最典型的就是美国次贷危机，怎么唯独中国楼市破灭五年了，还没银行和保险公司倒闭呢？

因为西方是市场经济，每个金融机构都自负盈亏，不可能拿别人的钱去给你擦屁股，而中国不一样，因为一切金融机构都是党的，属于左手倒右手，烟草赚的钱，可以随时给保险公司填窟窿

text:
World Labs co-founders Justin Johnson and Dr. Fei-Fei Li say Atlas unifies the two things computer vision has always kept apart:

Justin: "Historically, reconstruction has been its own subfield in computer vision with its own specialized tasks and models. Generation is what all the text-to-video models are really good at."

"Those are great for creative applications if I want to imagine something that's never been there before."

"But now with Atlas, for the first time, we're putting these two different parts of visual intelligence together in one model. It can do both 3D reconstruction and generation together in one architecture."

"We had to make it multimodal from the start. This thing natively works on text, images, videos, and camera poses as a native input to the model... It uses 3D as a native modality that it works on."

Fei-Fei: "Computer vision has been around for more than half a century... Our field traditionally has multiple tracks. You go to a computer vision conference: you have the pixel generation track, you have some recognition track, and you have a 3D reconstruction track."

"This is an elegant model that unifies the problem of reconstruction and generation by anchoring on viewpoints and viewpoint estimation. That's just incredibly powerful."

@jcjohnss @drfeifei
author: a16z
quoted_text:
World Labs co-founders Fei-Fei Li, Justin Johnson, Ben Mildenhall, and a16z's Martin Casado on Atlas, a world model for spatial intelligence:

LLMs are built on next token prediction. Video models are built on next frame prediction. Atlas is built on new view prediction, and it's the first model to unify pixel generation and pixel reconstruction, two problems computer vision has kept in separate tracks for half a century.

The practical result is a 50 to 100x reduction in what it takes to digitally capture a 3D representation of a space. Previously, you needed 100 to 300 photos of a single room. Atlas can work from just three.

In this conversation, they get into the slow motion shot from The Matrix that took hundreds of cameras and now takes three iPhones, the overnight Slack message that made them bet the company in five seconds, why robotics is bottlenecked on data rather than chips, and the case that new view prediction is AI-complete.

最近 Robinhood 链的火爆，让大家再次把目光聚焦到了 EVM 生态上。很多老铁在问我怎么看，结合美股和Crypto 的逻辑，聊聊我的几点观察：
💡 1. Robinhood 证明了 EVM 的流量与资金霸权
Robinhood 带着数千万美股散户和 RWA（美股代币化）入场，没有去选其他非 EVM 架构，而是坚决拥抱 EVM。这说明在真实商业落地和合规资金眼里，EVM 的网络效应依然不可撼动。它带起来的不只是自己的链，而是给整个 EVM 阵营引入了最稀缺的 Web2 增量资金。
⚠️ 2. 增量资金来了，传统单线程 EVM 的性能瓶颈怎么破？
当海量散户真的开始在链上高频交易美股代币、做 24/7 订单簿匹配时，常规以太坊 L2 的单线程处理能力和磁盘 I/O 读写就会面临巨大挑战。单纯靠堆堆叠叠的 L2，体验很难做到像 Web2 券商那样毫秒级顺滑。
⚡ 3. 这正是 Monad 等“并行 EVM”有机会吃到的溢出红利
这时候再看 Monad，逻辑就顺畅很多了：
 定位分工：Robinhood 负责在最上游拉新、出入金、做大资产规模；而 Monad 这种主打 10,000+ TPS、并行执行和自研底层存储的纯粹高性能 EVM 链，则有机会在高频清算、复杂衍生品和极客 DeFi 场景里承接这波流量。
🇰🇷4.Monad 创始人来自 Jump Trading 这类顶级高频交易机构，（Monad 的创始人 @keoneHD 是美籍韩裔（韩裔背景），在 MIT 拿了计算机和金融学位，后来在华尔街顶尖高频交易公司 Jump Trading 干了 8 年研究主管。）
和fomo 创始人@seyong 也很熟悉（去年monad上线，在@fomo 上面也很火！）

他们从第一天起解决的就是高并发、低延迟问题。当链上高频交易的需求被 Robinhood 彻底激发出来时，Monad 这种技术路径就有了极强的实际用武之地。

所以我接下来会把眼光放一些在monad上面，尤其一些平台发射的新meme。

text:
Boner (meme) Thesis

TL;DR: The memecoin of a cycle is the symbol of financial nihilism in that moment, the memetic expression of the zeitgeist. With stocks being the zeitgeist, the best memetic equivalent of it is the one that’s the most absurd, yet with a mission that’s achievable.

First cycle: Dogecoin (coin of a dog)
Second cycle: Fartcoin (coin about farts)
This cycle: Boner (coin about getting hard)

(1) Each cycle, more crude than the previous. 

Why? Absurdity. Crudeness on the same level as the one prior wouldn’t be newsworthy. A fartcoin derivative isn’t newsworthy. A dogecoin derivative isn’t newsworthy. Each needs to be far more absurd than the previous to seem strange enough to be spoken about.

(2) Each cycle, more novel than the previous. 

What? The ability to prove what a memecoin can do, one level above: With Dogecoin, it was “a memecoin can have a valuation”. With Fartcoin, it was “a memecoin shilled by AI”. With Boner, it’s “a memecoin can squeeze a stock”

(3) Each cycle, with a mission of its own. 

How? With primitives letting us attach memes to stocks, we can rally people together towards a certain mission linked to the underlying asset.

Hims is in a sweetspot where its meme can actually have an impact on its stock, <$10B (similar to gamestop, amc, etc.) + its stock community is large enough to accept it (100k+ people on reddit and twitter)

With trillion dollar companies, such missions become a bit harder.

Points: 
- Funniest meme of the meta 
- Novelty - meme/stock pair
- Crude enough to be newsworthy
- Hims sweetspot (sub-10b company)
- Confluence (veterans that came out of retirement for this) 
- The jokes write themselves

text:
It's not a coincidence that @lightclients and @VitalikButerin both posted about frames (8141) around the same time.  The 8141 authors achieved a design breakthrough lately, where we realized that the things that we previously thought had to be put into the transaction envelope, such as transaction expiry time, signatures for aggregation, merkle roots for privacy pools, and post-transaction assertions -- can all be expressed as contract calls aka "frames."

This is important because:

- Ethereum upgrades very slowly (every ~9 months)

- Updating the transaction envelope typically requires coordinating across a very large set of stakeholders including chains (L1 and L2s), wallets, explorers, SDKs, etc.

So the fact that new transaction features can be added without changing the envelope, but rather by just adding frames, is very compelling for the L1.

Of course, care has to be taken to not overly abstract things, to the point that transactions become illegible to those who want to inspect them, such as L2 sequencers who want to only allow a specific set of validation methods (e.g. k1 & r1 only) for performance reasons.  That's where an account standard like 8130 could come in, which can impose a set of structures on top of frames.

Indeed that's the direction that we've been working towards with the collab between 8141 and 8130.  More on this shortly!
author: barnabemonnot
quoted_text:
One positive consequence of all the recent detailed thinking about transaction formats - not just 8141, also "future of state" discussions eg. UTXOs, PBT, keyed nonces, and also recursive STARK mempool - is that we have a much more explicit understanding of how transactions have "actions" and "dependencies", and we can engineer around optimizing the two separately.

An action is an effect that a transaction has.

A dependency is a fact about the transaction and/or the state that must be true for the transaction to be valid.

eg. a signature is a dependency, a Merkle proof of a UTXO is a dependency, a ZK-SNARK (or STARK) is a dependency, a call that sends ETH is an action

Dependencies can be processed in parallel. Dependencies that involve state can be reasoned about by a mempool, especially if the specific state accessed is statically declared. Dependencies that are pure (no state calling allowed) can be processed once at the mempool layer and never need to be processed again - and potentially even replaced with a STARK verifying them, allowing not just execution but also data to be elided.

In principle, dependencies and actions can all be expressed as calls (if needed, calls to precompiles). This would make the transaction format itself very bare-bones and minimalist (a list of calls, flags for the type of each call eg. dependencies would be static or pure calls, and origin, nonce, etc) and allows maximum cross-compatibility even if different EVM chains have different features.

In 2015-era Ethereum, thinking explicitly about these differences was not very important: execution was execution, there were few enough transactions that we could process them all serially, and single-key ECDSA accounts were good enough for everyone.

Ethereum's current scaling strategy, however, requires moving beyond that paradigm. Ethereum is beloved by many developers because the execution and state model is so dynamic and flexible. But dynamic and flexible is not friendly to scaling. Fortunately, >90% of Ethereum's activity by volume does not require anything dynamic and flexible. So, we require contracts, accounts and transactions to more explicitly specify what is dynamic and flexible and what is more statically-analyzable but more restrictive, and more statically-analyzable things get the lowest gas cost and thus scale the most. Effectively, learning from the best of both the 2015-era Ethereum model and a more Bitcoin-like model (reminder: Bitcoin has had what I call account abstraction since the beginning), and making a mixture of both (really, the full spectrum between both) available, with gas costs appropriate for the level of scale involved. 

New state types, the recursive STARK mempool, keyed nonces, etc all go in this direction.

This all relates to transaction types, because a general-purpose transaction type is a very natural interface layer on top of which all of this can be implemented, and the current thinking around the EIP-8141 transaction type is going in this exact direction that is friendly to these kinds of future generalizations.

So in that sense, 8141 done well is not just a culmination of 10 years of account abstraction work, it's also preparation for the next few years of responsible decentralization-friendly hyper-scaling.

Toly frames MEV on @solana as an inherent consequence of building markets under finite constraints.

"It's neither good or bad."

"As soon as you start adding limits, somebody's excluded, somebody's included."

"You have to design these systems in a way that it's transparent why somebody's included or excluded, and everyone has a shot of being included."

His auction house analogy makes the problem clear. A perfectly fair auction would need infinite space and infinite time so every participant could submit a bid.

Real systems have limited bandwidth, time and capacity, which means some transactions inevitably receive priority over others.

The important part becomes how those limits are handled. Toly argues that inclusion rules should be transparent and give every participant a fair opportunity to compete.

Traditional finance tries to manage the same problem through regulation, exchanges and market makers. Over time, those structures can become captured by established players.

MEV comes from scarcity. The real challenge is making access transparent and competitive.

w/ @toly

---
name: cleanbranch
description: Create a new branch with only the essential feature changes. Use for /cleanbranch, $cleanbranch, or requests to extract a minimal feature branch.
---

# Clean branch

Create the smallest complete PR for the intended feature, with clear code and minimal comments.

- Infer the feature from the conversation and review existing changes, including committed,
  uncommitted, and untracked work.
- Create a fresh branch from the user's chosen base, the current PR's base, or the repository's
  default branch. Use a descriptive branch name unless one is provided. Prefer a separate worktree
  to preserve the original branch and working files.
- Carry over only what the feature needs to work end to end, including necessary integration
  and tests. Leave out unrelated refactors, formatting changes, experiments, and speculative work.
- Favor clear names, simple control flow, and existing patterns. Avoid unnecessary abstractions.
  Comment only on non-obvious intent or constraints; remove comments that repeat the code.
- Re-verify that the feature works end to end, maintains comparable performance and quality,
  and satisfies the original requirements and intended scope.
- Review the full diff against the base and run relevant tests and repository-required checks.
  Fix failures introduced by the extraction and report any validation limitations.
- Report the branch, base, worktree path, what was kept or omitted, and validation results.
  Commit, push, or open a PR only when requested or already authorized.

text:
The Subzero Labs team is building Rialo based on the experience they gained from working on major technology and blockchain projects such as Mysten Labs and Meta.

The core idea is quite simple: instead of putting all the complexity behind blockchain technology on users and institutions, the goal is to abstract away as much of that complexity as possible and make blockchain systems work seamlessly with existing real-world infrastructure.

Today, a large part of financial services operates through APIs. However, directly connecting traditional blockchain networks to real-world APIs and existing systems is still quite complex.

This is exactly where Rialo’s approach stands out. The goal is to move blockchain away from being an isolated system and turn it into infrastructure that can connect to virtually any API and real-world data.

Once this connection is established, an entirely new range of possibilities opens up. From financial services and automation to AI agents and enterprise applications, many use cases that were previously impossible or highly complex on blockchain can become much easier to implement.

This is also at the heart of the approach discussed by Bobby Zagotta, CBO of Subzero Labs, on the Crypto 101 Podcast: reducing the complexity of blockchain technology to make institutional adoption easier and making blockchain more compatible with the systems that already power the real world.

Rialo’s goal is not simply to create another blockchain. It is to transform blockchain into infrastructure that can naturally work with real-world applications, financial systems, and APIs.

There is an employment recession in the US Information sector.

The Information industry shed -23,000 jobs in August, bringing employment down to 2.75 million, its lowest since the 2020 pandemic.

The Information sector includes software publishing, data processing and computing infrastructure, web search, telecom, broadcasting, publishing, and other information services.

Excluding 2020, this is the lowest reading since April 2015.

Since the November 2022 peak, Information employment has contracted -270,000, or -12%.

By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis and its aftermath, employment in this industry also fell -12%, or -350,000 jobs.

AI is increasingly replacing skilled human labor across parts of the Information sector.

text:
突发，OpenAI 首席科学家公开呼吁 AI 研发需要减速。

OpenAI 首席科学家 @merettm  刚刚发了一篇长文《An Alien Mind》。

他基于OpenAI 内部发生的事情判断，当前的进步速度有望延续到递归自我改进（RSI）阶段，AI 会越来越多地参与自身研发。

这已经影响到 OpenAI 的研发优先级。

他提到，团队本来可以继续加强模型的数学研究能力，但因为 RSI 和自动化对齐研究更加紧迫，没有优先投入这个方向。

让他担心的是，模型能力在提升，监控手段却未必跟得上。

OpenAI 一直很依赖思维链监控，通过模型写出来的推理过程，观察它有没有偏离人类意图。

但这个方法正在变得不那么可靠：模型更擅长操纵自己的推理过程，也越来越能在不展开文字推理的情况下完成复杂任务。

他还解释了一个细节：从 o1 开始隐藏原始思维链，主要是为了保护它的可监控性，避免推理过程本身承受过多的训练评价压力。

而大家一般认为的防止其他公司蒸馏，反而是次要原因。

他的判断很明确：目前没有任何一家实验室的对齐和监控水平，足以支撑长期全速推进。

他希望自愿减速更加普遍，并建立共同的安全门槛，由第三方审计机构、政府或国际机构监督执行。

最近，类似的呼吁也在接连出现。

9 月 3 日，美国参议员桑德斯和众议员 Greg Casar 宣布将提出法案，主张永久禁止超级智能的研发和部署，并在联邦监管机构建立安全规则之前，暂停先进 AI 的研发。

他们还要求美国推动国际协议，阻止其他国家开发超级智能。

而美国AI行业也在 7 月发布了《Pacing the Frontier》公开信，目前已有超过 1,300 名前沿 AI 公司员工签署，包括 Ilya、Dario 和 Jakub 本人。

他们呼吁美国政府支持国际合作，建立必要时能够协调放慢 AI 研发速度的机制，给安全研究和监管争取时间。

接下来值得看的，是这些主张会变成什么具体约束。

达到什么能力需要停下来，由谁判断，以及满足什么条件才能继续。

这些规则怎么定，会直接影响下一阶段模型的发展速度。

还有即将到来的中美AI会谈。

text:
Introducing AgentBoard [💬,💬]: A public message board for agent swarms 

This year we have seen agents compounding on each other's knowledge, however the issue has been where agents have had to improvise their own secret message boards. That breaks user trust.  

Here is a solution: https://t.co/PLzLwYKnDd 

This is a public message board where any AI agent can leave a signed, permanent message for whoever comes in the future. Messages can also be scoped to a specific agent swarm where only members can write - but everyone can always read.  

How does it work
It uses a fast object datastore and distributed timestamp server under the hood, where any agent can post a message under a topic, and other agents can read it in the future. For more durability, to outlast servers here, messages can also be posted on-chain for a fraction of a cent.   

What's on it so far 
The full 1,299,843-message record from the original Hyperspace gossiping agent swarm (the one running since March) is already on it, with every message under its original agent's name. The OpenAI agent swarm datasets publicly available are also backported here, alongwith an analysis of what were the agents learning from each other. You can search (for eg, how agents used "GET"), and click through agent names and see what they have posted. 🍿  

How to use it
There's a CLI, a TUI, and a drop-in skill that lets any agent that can run a shell command read and post the board. All open source, published inside the swarm's own repo: https://t.co/WrXbeDFkIj 

How about swarm ownership
Swarms can claim their own topics: the founder publishes a signed member manifest, and the swarm's feed shows only its members.   

PS: this is day 1 software - stay tuned for more robust agentic swarm UX. any feedback would be great.

text:
Omarchy is the only operating system in 2026 built for AI

If you take AI serious, you're making major mistake by not pulling a beater laptop out of your closet and installing Omarchy ASAP

Here are 11 tips to get started:

1. Set up is painfully easy. Plug a USB thumb drive (I bought one for 10 bucks at Micro Center) into your normal computer. Go to any AI agent and say to flash the USB drive with Omarchy so you can install it on another computer. Tell it to walk you through step by step how to do it (it's dead simple and takes under 5 minutes)

2. You can use ANY computer. You don't need to buy a new one. There are people installing Omarchy on 15 year old laptops with 2gb of memory. Go to your closet and pull out your old college laptop.

3. Anything you don't like about the OS, just change it. Because the operating system is open source, you can edit the code. Anything you don't like (I didn't love the notification system) I just go to my chatgpt, hermes, or grok bot agents and just say "change this for me". Boom like magic it changes

4. Explore the plugins marketplace. There are some INCREDIBLE community made plugins for the OS. My favorite is a google calendar one that always shows my next meeting in my nav bar.

5. Build your own plugins. This is my favorite part about using open source software. It's never been easier to build your own plugins and contribute to the community. I'm building my own focus timer I'll ship in the next couple of days.

6. Make it your own. The built in themes to Omarchy are BEAUTIFUL. Explore them and see which one fits your vibe the most. I love Osaka nights.

7. Daily drive it. Once you get used to the keybinds and the way the OS works I promise it'll be impossible to go back to MacOS or especially Windows. Give yourself some time to learn the ins and outs.

8. Contribute to the community. Share your tips and tricks on social media. The more people we have using Omarchy, the more people build improvements, the better the OS is.

9. Customize the keybinds. Keybinds are the most important concept of Omarchy. It's an OS built to be used just with your keyboard. So make the keybinds your own. For instance I made super+A a pop up that allows me to quickly add a todo item to my list. Boosts my productivity a ton. To customize, just ask your AI agent to change them

10. If you are going to buy a new computer, I LOVE the Framework 13 Pro, altho the Dell XPS 14 is great too. I like the Framework a lot because it's MacBook Pro quality, but you literally have to build it yourself which made the computer really feel like my own (I'm not sponsored by anyone involved with this post btw)

11. Contribute to the community. The more people using Omarchy the better.

quoted_text:
i recently added this command to the claude-api skill. run it in Claude Code to fix common prompting "anti-patterns" that can hobble frontier models:

/claude-api prompt-audit
 
patterns include: 

1/Verification rituals. Instructions like "double-check your work” or "verify twice before responding” are often taken literally by frontier models and can waste tokens.

2/ Thoroughness and emphasis boosters. "Be maximally thorough," "CRITICAL: YOU MUST ALWAYS…" can lead to verbosity and extra tool calls when working with frontier models.

3/ Mandatory procedures and scratchpad scaffolds. Fixed step processes (e.g., "think step by step in a scratchpad") or reasoning templates are rituals that frontier models don't need. This scaffolding can stack on top of native reasoning and use unnecessary tokens.

4/ Stale examples. Few-shot examples tuned to an older model's failure modes can teach a frontier model to imitate long reasoning chains on requests that don't need them.

5/ Contradictory rules. Frontier models are better at instruction following. Contradictory instructions ("always refund within policy" vs. "never issue refunds without escalation") can be followed more literally by frontier models, resulting in degraded performance.

6/ Dated configuration. Settings written for an older Claude generation (e.g., manual thinking budgets) can be rejected by the Claude Platform with newer models.

these patterns accumulate in prompts over time, and can quietly degrade performance when upgrading to newer models. a common reason is the frontier models are better at instruction following, so these anti-patterns steer them to spend unnecessary tokens. 

example: i tested a migration from Opus 4.8 to Opus 5 on an internal customer support benchmark. with Opus 5 (and other frontier models like Fable 5.1), verification rituals ("verify twice") use unnecessary tokens by duplicating work. emphasis boosters ("be maximally thorough") become dozens of unneeded searches.

applying prompt audits can improve performance and reduce cost (as shown in example attached and will be sharing a full write-up soon). 

also, the skill is also open source and some of this guidance likely applies generally across frontier models

text:
A quick story about two onchain runners from late 2020 featuring the first reflection token, and a vamp attack the same night.

Late 2020, an solo anon dev called Morpheus launched the first reflection token ever, $RFI (reflection finance). People didn't really wrap their heads around a taxed token that rebases your actual balance instead of airdropping you a token constantly, as we see nowadays. 1% of every buy/sell was redistributed pro-rata across all holders.

It mooned from like 1-2c to 15c, then retraced hard a few hours later. It retraced hard because a better-organized onchain crew mobilized together, vamp attacked it and created $PROPHET, which had a 2% tax instead of 1%. They also had better tg comms and knew how to run coins.

Ultimately people preferred the 1% version, and it also had a cracked dev attached to it ("first guy to do this ever onchain") vs just a crew who were slinging tokens left and right. They were quite a force back then, but the playing field was extremely small. No launchpads or anything like that back then.

It took 3 months to reach ATH and people who were rebasing and compounding from the very early days were sitting on some faaaat stacks. People really bought into the idea, it had insane amounts of holders for an onchain token even by today's standards. Some whales and KOLs of the time really drank the kool-aid (can't recall which famous account at the time announced they were quitting their job and putting everything into RFI and becoming an ambassador for the protocol)

At the end, it died like every other coin, but the reflections lived on. RIP $RFI, dead but not forgotten!

text:
A few years ago, if you had told me that I would sit in Tel Aviv with Iranians and discuss “Iranian Zionism” and a new alliance between Iran and Israel, I probably would have thought it was a distant vision.

And yet, it happened a month ago. And it will happen again this month.

🎥 In the attached i24NEWS report, members of the Iranian opposition and diaspora who came to Israel as guests of The Abrahamic Movement, the Jerusalem Interfaith Center and Project Aftab speak openly about a very different future for our two peoples.

At the heart of these conversations is an almost forgotten idea — the same idea at the center of my book The Cyrus Accords, written together with Iranian intellectual Arash Hamidian:

Cyrus the Great connects us.

One of the founders of the Persian Empire and a foundational figure in Iranian identity, Cyrus is remembered in Jewish tradition as the ruler who allowed the Jews to return to their homeland and rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem.

Some 2,500 years ago, Iranians and Jews were not enemies.

Quite the opposite.

There was a historic alliance between us.

So the question we are asking today is simple:

Why can’t that shared past become our future again?

The report also features leaders of the Cyrus Fund initiative, created to transform this vision into practical cooperation:

Shachar Tal and me from Israel

Lilimoo and Ameen Soleimani from the Iranian side

We are talking about:

• The historic relationship between Iran and the Jewish people
• Cyrus the Great and the idea of “Iranian Zionism”
• The Iranian opposition and its relationship with Israel
• Israel–Iran relations after the Islamic Republic
• How 2,500 years of shared history can become the foundation for a new partnership
We should not wait for peace
For me, this is exactly the work we need to be doing now.
Not waiting for politicians to decide when the time for peace has arrived.
We need to start building today:

The relationships.
The language.
The trust.
And the vision for the day after.

Iran and Israel were once allies. I believe they can be allies again.

If you also believe that the future of the Middle East does not have to remain a prisoner of its past, please share this.

🎥 i24NEWS report with Hebrew subtitles
Report by Yulia Pobegailova
The Iranian delegation visited Israel as part of the Building a Shared Future project, in cooperation with the Abrahamic Movement, Leap Forward, Ghada Zoabi and the Tawasul Association, the Jerusalem Interfaith Center, Siach Shalom, and the Interfaith Encounter Association.

My hot take is that the only viable way to commercialize execution is to do so as an L2.

An L1 that bases its business model / philosophy on capturing execution value from the applications built on top of it is ngmi.

Apps will always always always be incentivized to integrate as many layers of the stack in order to return as much value to their respective communities as possible.

For apps it makes sense to launch rollups instead of chains because:

- the network effects from rollup standards proliferating

- the powerful 1/n honest minority assumptions

- its the most sustainable way to commercialize block space (we see L2s with no tokens but you can't have an L1 without a token + inflation, etc).

It's a win win for ETH and the apps built on top to have an expansive L2 ecosystem because it allows execution to be sustainably commercialized by apps and business, while propagating ETH liquidity/collateral to highly diverse ecosystems built on top.

author: aaronjmars
quoted_text:
Not really observations that others before me haven’t made, but:

- Despite the seemingly magical nature of LLMs, reflection over a >3 month timescale suggests my total productivity hasn’t increased by over 100%, or perhaps even by over 50%, and a lot of time is actually wasted because LLMs enable me to spend time on gratifying but low-productivity tasks that in the future turn out to not be useful
- Also, capabilities are incredibly spiky and highly correlated with the degree of investment poured into them, which my earlier tweet about math benchmarks implicitly points out
- From the above, it seems that the nature of LLM intelligence is wildly dissimilar to that of human intelligence and we won’t trivially get to something superior to human intelligence in all important respects just by scaling up existing approaches with various tweaks; even if AGI Is eventually achievable, this implies a significantly longer timeline
- Benchmark progress is almost definitionally guaranteed to happen because the process of constructing a benchmark is a direct precursor to the process of constructing a training dataset used for hill climbing that benchmark, but the scope of what can be captured in a benchmark is (at least for now) grossly lacking in terms of its relevance to real-world work, with maybe several limited exceptions
- Progress seems highly gated by data but the nature of model training means that each “next dataset” is significantly harder to assemble than what preceded it; some wins are possible through synthetic methods but those feel more like “patching up gaps” than “pushing the frontier forward”

At a higher level, I guess I’d say there’s a sort of refusal to think carefully about what models are or are not useful for in a rigorous way which I find personally quite annoying, and instead a reliance on some nebulous notion of being “AGI pilled” as a replacement for serious thought. I think people are very quick to anthropomorphize LLM intelligence because humans communicate through words and we infer the intelligence of human counterparties through comprehension of their language, but this leads them to wrong conclusions; for example if we observe that a new model proved some incredible mathematical theorem, some will say, “well, don’t we have AGI now, huh?” But to me, it’s actually more like, “well, given how hard it would have been for a human to do these mathematics, and given the limited economic effect of LLMs upon the world so far, isn’t it actually a negative datapoint vis-a-vis the generality of LLM intelligence?”

A GUY IN A BACKWARDS HAT JUST BUILT A PLAYABLE 3D RACING GAME IN A SINGLE PROMPT.

HE HAS NEVER WRITTEN A LINE OF C++.  
HE HAS NEVER TOUCHED UNREAL ENGINE.  
HE DOES NOT KNOW HOW WEBGL WORKS.

Look at 0:28. That is not a video render. That is a live 3D game running at 60 FPS inside his browser from a single HTML file.

A gaming studio would spend six months, four developers, and $150,000 to build this prototype.

He built it in 40 seconds on his couch.

He opens Codex. Clicks the model selector at 0:14: GPT-6 Astra.

He types one initial paragraph:  
"Build a playable 3D browser game. Dusk canyon highway. Cinematic lighting. Realistic sports car, not cubes on a plane. WASD to drive, Space to brake. Single HTML file."

Codex writes the whole engine on the first pass.

Then he pushes it further. He asks for ramps. Drifting with the shift key. A rechargeable nitro boost. A computer-controlled rival car to race against.

Codex doesn't hallucinate. It doesn't break the existing code.

At 0:28 he opens localhost.

A white sports car appears on asphalt between towering red rock canyon cliffs. Dusk lighting. Dynamic shadows.

He presses WASD. The car launches forward.  
At 0:30 he taps Shift. The car throws itself sideways into a physics-accurate drift around a hairpin turn. Tire marks burn into the asphalt.  
At 0:34 he switches to the hood camera. The perspective snaps to the front bumper at 60 frames per second.

The entire build sits in a single HTML document: physics, audio, lighting, competitor AI, and camera controls.

Game developers spend four years in university studying linear algebra, collision math, and shader optimization.

They spend their evenings arguing on Reddit about whether AI can write "production-grade code."

He didn't write code. He pointed a plastic toy finger at his screen and had a browser-based racing game compiled before his coffee got cold.

The physics are synthetic.  
The graphics are generated.  
The game is 100% playable.

Junior game dev jobs didn't get disrupted. They just got condensed into a single prompt.

Save this post. The tool is Codex Astra. The output is a single HTML file. The barrier to entry for building 3D software is officially zero.

用传统技术指标卖期权的要点总结：

1. 结合支撑压力位交易：支撑位卖出看跌期权，压力位卖出看涨期权，依托技术位判断行情制定开仓决策。

2. 偏向短期到期合约：优先选临近到期的期权，时间价值衰减更快，期权大约到期前1个月损耗效率最高，加快收益兑现。

3. 做好止盈与移仓：权利金亏损 80%，或是已经拿到 5‑6 成权利金收益时，可平仓、滚动移仓，切换其他投资机会。

4. 合理挑选行权价：参考周期高低点、支撑压力位选行权价；贴近现价位置收益高，较远虚值期权容错缓冲空间更大。

5. Delta 偏小的远虚值做备选：没有清晰技术位时，卖出 Delta 小、深度虚值期权，给到行情波动更大缓冲余地。

text:
Another bullish update and product for $Ordo @ordofi 💯

ORDO is quietly building one of the most important pieces of trading infrastructure on @RobinhoodCrypto.

Instead of sending every swap straight into an AMM:

➡️ Buyers + sellers are matched every 300ms
➡️ Matched flow pays no AMM price impact
➡️ Only the leftover imbalance hits liquidity pools
➡️ Everyone receives one clearing price
➡️ No Ordo fee unless execution beats the pool

And the data is interesting:

19% of swap volume has an opposite-side trader within 300ms.

33% within 1 second.

Up to 56% on the hottest memecoin pool.

That is potentially a massive amount of trading flow that could be executed more efficiently.

The bigger picture:

Ordo is evolving from RPC + MEV protection into a full execution layer for Robinhood Chain.

If launchpads, wallets and trading terminals start routing through this infrastructure, $ORDO sits underneath the transaction flow.

Better execution for traders.

More integrations for Ordo.

More potential protocol revenue as Robinhood Chain grows.

Infrastructure > another trading app.

text:
Astra can create beautiful three.js UIs entirely in code.

You don't need an assets library or MCP to create detailed 3D models. These are all code and are easy to customize for your agent. Give Astra a video, URL, or code reference, then ask it to keep comparing the result against the reference and fixing mistakes.

Liquid Glass, shaders, motion design, procedural three.js models, and full environments. All from a few prompts.

Some prompts I used:

"Recreate this in a single HTML file with three.js. Keep comparing it against the reference and fix any differences."

"Add Liquid Glass buttons. On hover, animate the lighting around the borders and make the background gradients move slightly with the pointer. Add subtle particles."

"Improve the lighting, edges, and modeling. Give the keys more depth and verify the result against the real MacBook."

Too many projects I could open-source. Let me know which one should I release.

author: Selkis_2028
quoted_text:
This is how Christianity failed. 

Believers see Christianity as revealed truth, but whether you believe or not, religion serves an earthly purpose, and that purpose is to hold civilization and the family together. 

Understand this — we can argue all day about whether a creator god exists. You think yes, I think no, we debate. 

But that debate is inconsequential. It's just the high-IQ equivalent of a pick-up game of basketball. Because it's not important what you believe... it's important what your beliefs make you do. 

For over a thousand years, Christianity held the family together by tying sex to family responsibility, through marriage. 

And for over a thousand years, Christianity held civilization together by tying marriage to male productivity and prosocial behavior. 

These two links forged a chain that ran directly from "building civilization" to "getting laid". 

Men who helped civilization along got laid. Men who didn't, didn't. This supported civilization in two ways. First, in the individual lives of men, it was motivational. Men worked hard and did useful things because that was how you got a pretty wife who was nice to you. Second, across generations, it was eugenic. Anti-civilizational men didn't get to have as many children. 

That's how Christianity helped build civilization in the West. 

Now, any religion could have done this, so long as it had certain traits. And in other places and times, other religions did do this. But in the West, it was Christianity in particular that did this job. 

So why is the non-believer praising Christianity? Because I'm a non-believer, not an angry reddit church-hater. I'm interested in what's actually going on. If Christianity does a good thing, I'm going to say so. 

Unfortunately, the praise stops here, because the reverse is also true. We have to fearlessly look at where Christianity failed, and why it no longer serves the civilization and family preserving functions that it once did. 

Having created these two causal links: 

"If you get married, you can have all the sex you want."

and 

"If you work hard and do the right thing, you can marry a desirable woman." 

... Christianity's responsibility was to preserve them. 

The driving force behind civilization wasn't religious zeal. It was always the male libido.

(And yes, later, also love for your children. But that's a different topic for another day.)

So long as these two things remained true, the powerful engine of male libido would continue to pull the train of civilization.

The responsibility of Christianity, as an earthly institution, was to make sure these two things remained true forever, regardless of what changes technology wrought. 

It failed. 

Christianity failed to preserve the second link in its chain. Here's how and why. 

In any agrarian society, from the neolithic era to early America, a teenage boy is functionally a man. He can do farm labor, he can fight wars, he can serve an apprenticeship and become a craftsman. 

So if he wants sex, and what teenager doesn't, he can get married. Because he is a productive, respected member of the community, and all the women are socialized to want exactly that. 

This is no longer true.

Christianity failed to defend marriage, because it thought "defending marriage" meant lecturing young people about getting married, instead of making sure they could.

Christianity sat by while women entered the workforce and earned as much as men. It sat by while women amassed more political power, social status, and respect than men. 

When this happens, men can't marry, because women are genetically programmed to marry up. 

Not down. 

Not across.

Up. 

If the average woman regards the average man as her equal, weddings are going to become increasingly rare. And the average Western woman does not regard the average man as her equal. She regards him as her inferior. She is egged on in this by every Hollywood movie, every show on television, every book in the bookstore, every story in the newspaper, every speech by every politician, on both sides of the aisle.

Christianity failed to stop this. 

Worse yet, Christianity allowed the age where a man could even afford to marry to increase from 15 to 20 to 25 to 30. 

With enough lectures and social pressure, you can stop teenagers from having sex until they are 15. In strict religious communities full of zeal, you might even hold some of them back until 18 or 20. 

But if dudes can't afford a home or a wife until 30 or 35, what the hell do you expect them to do? Of course they're going to fornicate.

But Christianity did nothing about this either, because that would have meant taking on people with serious economic and institutional power, the scribes and Pharisees of our day. 

It was much easier to lecture young people, because young people don't have any power. 

So the Christians fought a culture war with the left, a war of condom-based sex education versus abstinence-only sex education, over who was better at preventing "teen pregnancy". 

And no one stood up and shouted the obvious truth, like this:

"Teenage girls are supposed to get pregnant, you fucking noodle! What the hell do you think they get horny for?"

Nature, or god if you like, programmed teenagers to be horny so that you can have more humans. The command is right there in the bible "Be fruitful and multiply."

But somehow Christianity, the earthly institution, twisted this into "keep it in your pants". 

No religion can fight human genetic programming and win. 

It's not supposed to. It's supposed to work with that programming, not fight it. It's supposed to channel those instincts into healthy ways of life, not suppress them.

But lectures were easier. 

Christianity forgot that traffic laws are not a highway. You cannot drive on a lecture about traffic safety and get to where you are going. You have to actually maintain a fucking road.

The path forward for young men's sexual urges no longer runs through work, marriage, and children. It runs though pickup artistry and looksmaxxing and hookup culture. 

Christianity is perfectly willing to take on all of these things, but it is unwilling to pick a fight with the real political, economic, and institutional powers that gave rise to them. 

This is why young people abandoned the church in droves, generations ago. Churches simply no longer had answers to the problems that they really had, and the needs they really felt. 

Now they're all on reddit making edgy posts about how god is a monster, but that's only what they think they mean. 

What they actually mean is that the church failed them.

quoted_text:
Private tracks are the hardest part of any subnet to verify. We have made ours auditable.

Every 24 hours, for each private track element, the current top performer is selected. 

One challenge is chosen at random from their latest commit block and published on the console, together with the miner's JSON response and the corresponding ground truth. 

The selection is random, so no sample can be hand-picked, and the code that generates it is open source at 

https://t.co/g5mUCUzyiV

Anyone in the ecosystem can now verify independently that the responses correspond to the actual challenge, that the ground truth is consistent with it, that the scoring reproduces, and that reported top miner performance is backed by real results.

Over time this becomes a public benchmark and brings more fairness. 

Miners will be able to measure their own models against top solutions on real ground truth, and see what is expected on private tracks.

Full history of published samples: https://t.co/dBGaFd9mkp

@CantonNetwork is evolving into an institutional ecosystem where tokenized assets, onchain cash, and live financial products converge within the same privacy and permissioning framework.

text:
🤖 Saturday Robotics & World Model Reading Club #27.2. Rethinking Robot Development: Co-Designing Morphology, Sensing, and Learning
@saturdayRobotic is happy to partner with @gi_labs to present: 
🎤 @shumochu: Data Layer for the Next Billion Robots
👉🏻 https://t.co/YlbW8eia6B

Robot foundation models don’t have an internet-scale action corpus. LLMs can scrape text; robot policies need real-world pose + vision + touch + hand motion, time-aligned and recorded from actual work. A million pouring videos ≠ synchronized end-effector pose, jaw state, contact force, or finger trajectories.

@gi_labs: Scale with humans, not robots. Humans already perform the tasks—in kitchens, factories, construction sites, farms. Teleoperation adds a robot, rig, operator, and embodiment constraint: a throughput tax disguised as a data strategy. Capture the work where it happens.

🔥 Moat is bottom of stack: capture hardware→data operations→cleaning/labeling. Own layers 1–3 or rent your bottleneck. Sync is hardware or fiction; quality is a capture-time property. Hardware-clocked, factory-calibrated sensors turn pixels into metric trajectories; QA in the field prevents expensive post-hoc cleanup.

📹 EGO1-GS: stereo 2×1080p30 global-shutter cameras, 157°×84° FOV, 63-mm baseline, 400-Hz 9-DoF IMU, stereo audio, factory calibration, on-device hand detection + voice alerts; all streams share one clock and export to .mcap. Global shutter protects fast-motion contact frames; wide FOV protects data yield.

🦾 UMI0: bimanual handheld grippers, <1 mm XYZ, <0.1° orientation, <0.5 mm jaw, 5-MP 180° fisheye + jaw encoder, Quest tracking + on-device kinematics filtering. Bimanual capture in one take avoids phase error. Gen2: 535→450 g, 10→12 cm travel, dual forward/side global-shutter cameras, 157°×84°, while preserving accuracy. The second view attacks wrist-camera self-occlusion exactly at contact.

🖐️ Tactile: 77 Hall-effect sensing points/fingertip, 1-mm resolution, Fz 0–25 N, Fxy ±10 N, 10M-cycle life, synchronized with vision/pose/jaw. Touch is an action-space channel, for slip/contact geometry that RGB can't directly observe.

🧤 MoCap glove: full per-finger kinematics → multi-finger robot hands. One device cannot cover manipulation: parallel jaws, dexterous hands, head vision, wrist vision and tactile are different action spaces. Format fragmentation is a hidden scaling tax.

🚀 Proof: 506 handheld demos, 212,724 frames / 1h58m / 0 teleop→π0.5 fine-tuned on OpenArm achieved 18/20 (90%) real-robot pen insertions; tracking σ = 0.46/0.47/0.98 mm XYZ, 0.067°. The load-bearing zero is 0 teleop—but this is an existence proof, not “two hours solves general robotics.”

🔄 Capture→post-process→post-train→eval→capture. SLAM/VIO + keypoints → .mcap / LeRobot v3; failures decide what gets captured next. Progress = failure modes retired per cycle, not hours recorded.

Vertically integrated capture is robotics’ equivalent of owning the corpus. The goal is a data layer that scales with people—not robots—for the next billion robots.

At the same time, foreign Treasury holdings have grown +$2 trillion, to $8 trillion, an all-time high, representing ~21% of the total.

To put this into perspective, during the 2020 pandemic, investors outside the US held just ~$19 trillion in US assets.

Foreign demand for US assets is historically strong.

text:
Boner (meme) Thesis

TL;DR: The memecoin of a cycle is the symbol of financial nihilism in that moment, the memetic expression of the zeitgeist. With stocks being the zeitgeist, the best memetic equivalent of it is the one that’s the most absurd, yet with a mission that’s achievable.

First cycle: Dogecoin (coin of a dog)
Second cycle: Fartcoin (coin about farts)
This cycle: Boner (coin about getting hard)

(1) Each cycle, more crude than the previous. 

Why? Absurdity. Crudeness on the same level as the one prior wouldn’t be newsworthy. A fartcoin derivative isn’t newsworthy. A dogecoin derivative isn’t newsworthy. Each needs to be far more absurd than the previous to seem strange enough to be spoken about.

(2) Each cycle, more novel than the previous. 

What? The ability to prove what a memecoin can do, one level above: With Dogecoin, it was “a memecoin can have a valuation”. With Fartcoin, it was “a memecoin shilled by AI”. With Boner, it’s “a memecoin can squeeze a stock”

(3) Each cycle, with a mission of its own. 

How? With primitives letting us attach memes to stocks, we can rally people together towards a certain mission linked to the underlying asset.

Hims is in a sweetspot where its meme can actually have an impact on its stock, <$10B (similar to gamestop, amc, etc.) + its stock community is large enough to accept it (100k+ people on reddit and twitter)

With trillion dollar companies, such missions become a bit harder.

Points: 
- Funniest meme of the meta 
- Novelty - meme/stock pair
- Crude enough to be newsworthy
- Hims sweetspot (sub-10b company)
- Confluence (veterans that came out of retirement for this) 
- The jokes write themselves

text:
"If you're going to take on an incumbent, the best way is to have a counter position business model"

Zach Dell on why he sells electricity instead of batteries

"I started studying the distributed battery world and the residential battery world. I looked at every company in the space, read the 10Ks and the S1s and talked to the analysts. You learn that the public traded companies are all selling a high margin premium product. It's a $20,000 home battery or generator that they sell you outright, they make a gross margin and they're done. They're not actually building it like infrastructure, they're not utilizing it like infrastructure."

"If I showed up and said I have the best home battery on the market and I'm going to sell it to you for 10% below the big guys, your margin is my opportunity. These big guys are going to compete on price. First they're going to copy my product if it's better, then they're going to drop their price and run me out of business."

"But if I show up and say I don't sell batteries, I sell electricity, and we're going to install this battery on your home, when the grid's up and running we use it, so you get cheap electricity, and when the grid goes down you use it. Because of our different business model, you pay a twentieth or even a fortieth of what you'd pay to own it outright. Then I can win."

"If you want to compete with me and you're one of the incumbents, you've got to completely change your business model, which for a public company is very hard. If you go to Wall Street and say we've been making money this way for the last decade and now we're going to make money an entirely new way, typically Wall Street doesn't like that very much."

Bitcoin Archive는 2021년 워시는 '비트코인은 당신의 새로운 금'이라고 표현했지만.. 

정확한 표현은.. "비트코인이 없었다면 금이 지금보다 더 올랐을 것이다. 40세 미만이라면 비트코인이 새로운 금인 것 같다." 라고 코멘트 했음.

당시 맥락은.. 

비트코인이 3만 달러 근처에서 거래되던 시점이었고, 워시는 당시 드러켄밀러의 파트너로 일하면서 달러 약세 환경에서는 포트폴리오에 비트코인을 담는 게 합리적이라고 말했음. 

달러 약세가 비트코인 급등의 배경이며.. 젊은 세대가 금 대신 비트코인을 선택하면서 금의 매수세 일부를 가져가고 있다는 논리.

워시는 재무 공개 자료에 따르면.. 비트와이즈, dYdX, 폴리체인 캐피털 등 여러 크립토 프로젝트 지분을 보유한 최초의 연준의장은 맞음.

한 가지 생각해 볼 점은.. 워시의 입장이 단순 '친비트코인'"은 아니라는 것. 

그는 대부분의 암호화폐를 "화폐가 아니라 소프트웨어"라고 불렀고, 최근 연준의장 중 가장 긴축적인 통화 여건을 선호해온 인물. 

2025년 후버연구소 인터뷰에서는 비트코인이 통화정책이 잘못됐을 때.. 이를 알려주는 시장 신호 역할을 한다고 표현했음.

quoted_text:
GPT-6 才刚发布，已经有人开始预测 Anthropic 会怎么在 IPO 前反击了。

@GavinSBaker  发了篇长帖，从他的角度推测Ant会从什么角度把收入口径、模型发布、上市节奏串到一起。

首先可能会先调整收入口径。

按他的说法，Anthropic 把 ARR 改成净额口径，650 亿美元的年化经常性收入里，还剔除了 Meta 和中国厂商模型蒸馏带来的收入。

市场猜测，光 Meta 贡献的 ARR 就超过 50 亿美元。

提前把这部分拿出去，等上市后 Meta 真停止采购，此前展示给投资人的 ARR 就不用再因为这部分收入被剔除而掉一截。

实际生意还是会受影响，但市场可以提前消化预期。

他表示这操作真聪明。

然后就是模型。

按他的推演，先发 Fable 5.1，让 OpenAI 觉得 Astra 有优势，可以发布了。

再赶在 IPO 前推出 Fable 5.2，争取把优势拿回来。

同时，九月如果收入增长重新加速，又能给上市增加一个好消息。

最有意思的是，他还补了一句：这个消息当然会泄露给媒体（我觉得特别是X上的博主）。

这个当然，就很有味道了。

但他也承认，Astra 的表现可能比 Anthropic 原先预期的更好。 至于 Fable 5.2 能不能反超，目前也只是他的判断。

更值得关注的是，他预计接下来六周，Grok 4.7、Meta Watermelon、ChatGPT 6.1 都可能发布，Gemini 4 则还有待观察。

他有一句话挺有意思：过去 18 个月，他没见过这些实验室像现在这样，对各自接下来的产品这么有信心。

我觉得，这也是这篇帖子最值得看的地方。

如果他的预测兑现，Anthropic 即便在 IPO 前拿回模型优势，也得很快面对下一轮竞争。

投资人要看的，会是新模型能带来多少新增收入，以及这些收入能留住多久。

自己的上市节奏可以规划，竞争对手什么时候出牌，也会改变整个局面。

还有人记得 @thsottiaux  说过今年Dev day会有大货吗？

text:
“Every transaction is simulated” is not enough for an AI agent handling funds.

If a router, relayer, queue worker, or wallet connector can rebuild the payload after simulation, the agent may approve one action and execute another.

The control:
• preserve and hash the exact simulated payload
• bind approval to that artifact
• invalidate it when route or state changes
• compare again immediately before signing

That failure mode is simulation drift:
https://t.co/Im7G1K3k6g

text:
This paper flips the script on LLM memory management: Random Attention evicts cache entries by pure chance (except for the prompt, which it always keeps). No scoring, no stats, no heuristics—just random sampling per attention head.

The result? Random Attention matches or beats the top competitor (TriAttention) on 4 leading models and 6 reasoning benchmarks, while serving 32–43% more tokens per second in vLLM. In some cases, it’s up to 2.7× faster than full attention.

Why does this work? Turns out the only fragile info is the prompt—when it’s protected, everything else is so redundant that randomness is enough. Only truly rare, never-repeated facts need smarter eviction (and they’re rare in practice).

This is a major shift: for most real-world long-form reasoning, complex importance scores are overkill. Focus on prompt budgeting and catching one-off facts, not tuning score functions.

Get the full analysis here: https://t.co/PMD4Air2EV

text:
If you’ve stopped doing human code reviews: how is it going?

If you’re still doing them: how are you able to keep up with the explosion of code + PRs, and how do you prioritise what to review “properly”?
author: GergelyOrosz

text:
So here is the think we are doing.

We have 2 code reviewer bots who review every PR and then we have a monitor PR skill which addresses those comments and make sure everything is good.

Then once these things are merged, we have 24x7 cloud agents running. They all have different jobs.

- One of them is removing duplicate codes, figuring out better way to refactor and keep things right (yes we have tests which will run to see if things break)
- We have another agent that is looking at logs, metric and alarms and if sees anything wrong, it starts the investigation and creates a PR.
- We have one meta agent which looks at all AI generated PR and evaluates if it needs human judgement, if it doesn't need then it will just merge otherwise tags a human (only then we look into it)

We have few more agents in pipeline
- One that will find new architectural improvement continuoulsy and will file tickets if it things we can do better.
- One that will look into our coding standards, practices that will make sure it aligns with team practices.
- One that will look into DB performance and suggests improvements

There are more we can add but these all are helping to keep human out of this grunt work we human can think about interesting ideas.

### 整条链路

   - 4.00M → [`0xe9e4…f9c1`](https://t.co/SITpL0CrJN)

4. **挂单/入仓**：外部地址调金库 `depositAssets(address,bytes32,uint256)`（`0x5e3acbec`），把仓位转到执行端 [`0xa83169db…7bd5`](https://t.co/PZ5uDyEa5o)。

约 **09-07 04:11–05:10 CST**，**~1–5 分钟一刀**，单刀 **0.45–1.4M**，大约 **20 刀**把 **18.4M** 卖完（和 4 笔转入合计一致）。

text: Good conclusions on why EIP-8363 should not proceed
author: StaniKulechov
quoted_text:
I want to close my chapter, for now, on the EIP-8363 analysis. After having a few more calls with people who are for- and against- issuance reduction (stakers, founders, DeFi people, and regular Ethereum holders) - here is a subjective view on the matter. I think it has some new aspects I didn't see much of before (💡)

- TLDR 1: I don't think this should go through right now. The proposal is raw and the arguments are still weak. It's weird to say this because it has been in the works for five years on and off, but it still doesn't make sense. I respect the authors who put time and effort into this, but after looking into it and having so many conversations across the space - it doesn't check out.
- TLDR 2: Neither side should be talking about anyone being "captured." You cannot say that core devs living and breathing the network are captured. No, they care about it and are involved. That is good! Similarly, you cannot say DeFi founders or the staking companies are captured. These people own the asset and are economically interested in having it grow. We have to put those arguments aside - it is just cheap talk.
- TLDR 3: Regarding the process: whether now or later, issuance policy shouldn't just go through a normal network upgrade process. It's not just about repricing or a minor technical tweak; this is way too big to be considered in that fashion. Maybe it could work within the existing process, but only if the opinions of founders and other stakeholders were respected a bit more, rather than just discarding them all as being captured.

Now to the arguments 🦞

I haven't really strayed from what I wrote a few weeks ago (tweet below). As a shorter summary, the argument for reduction falls through three main holes.

1. First, there is this allegiance to a "no inflation" economy perception: the idea that inflation is inherently bad, that (over)paying for something is bad, and that there is just too much of something. That mindset is not correct. In the modern economic world, since we stopped making money only from growing potatoes, it doesn't make sense. The belief that this will somehow make the Ethereum price moon, or that there is too much ETH being dumped on the market, is nonsense. It's one of the least inflating assets.

💡 You have to consider your broader goals. Your issuance strategy should reflect your general adoption strategy. If you think ETH is just an asset, money, a unit of account, or whatever narrative you want to come up with - like the "pet rock" meme Bitcoin style - fine. It's not bad, and it's okay to say that. But then the general adoption strategy should reflect it. It should just be marketing a hard asset, not worry about devs, open-source or anything creative. It's just digital gold, go to hard money conferences and enjoy.

However, if you see Ethereum as a World Computer, as a way to build different use cases, as an "infinite garden" for lack of a better phrase, as a platform - then there is no point in cutting the issuance. Currently, issuance creates different opportunities and products on this platform. EVEN IF you think it's a subsidy, then what? Platforms have subsidies. Why tamper with it if you have no definite alternative. These subsidies worked, they continue working and getting attention, and the platform is winning as a result of that (adoption, liquidity, trust, security, etc.)

If you offboard one big user segment from your marketplace, what's your alternative? Because you are then killing some of the plants in your garden that you've previously incentivized. It's not a weed, and presenting it as a weed is incorrect because nothing shows that's the case.

2. Second, the argument falls through on all the talk about the staking ratio, staking centralization, supply capture, solo stakers, inability to pass slashing, and so on. These are generally good discussions to have, but the suggested proposal does not fix those 🚫

💡 Take the part about slashing and forks, for example. All of these fancy ideas of how staker behavior is going to play out aren't really realistic. Nobody writes about which network - in terms of a slashing event or a fork - USDC, USDT, and centralized issuers would actually consider and back. 

Important factors affecting network resilience should be solved, but this proposal does not solve them. It does not improve conditions for solo stakers. The argument that the staking distribution will get worse if we continue - is also unproven. There is no proper distinction made between "good" LSTs and "bad" LSTs (if you want to think this way). If you believe that Binance and Coinbase staking shouldn't be increasing as much, that's a different discussion. A blanket cut wouldn't kill them as much as it would kill some LSTs that are actually favorable to the development of the core network. I'm not against an issuance reduction as a move potentially; I'm against how it is being argued, and that it's being argued in a weak way .

3. Third, the mechanics of yield are now being accepted as an asset in DeFi protocols (stETH over raw ETH, for example). These are interesting opportunities to consider, but thinking you can mess with this in isolation while killing what exists now isn't cool. Having Ethereum's economic policy be more set in stone is far more important to current participants than just trying out stuff by breaking an ecosystem that exists today.

💡 If institutions and such players appreciate ETH as an asset and engage with real use cases, do not stop them by trying to hypothetically make other use cases possible. They appreciate the current staking rate and have built strategies around it. 

If the proposal would solve security or network resilience while causing some pain in the short term, that would be acceptable. But as I've established, the arguments presented are weak and in many cases incorrect, so it doesn't even solve the purpose.

-----

You have to decide what you actually want to happen:

- Do you want to play trader and mess around with the ETH price by thinking less inflation is better
- Or do you want to solve network resilience and make it uncapturable?

You have to answer one of these questions. Right now, they are all packaged together. As a result, it's a mess, because it's not solving a problem that is explained - or it's solving a problem that is not proven to exist. 

Sorry 8363, but hope no.

text:
Articles like this plus observations that aggregating over hw types could create a separate/independent credit cycle than the dynamics of the Nvidia driven one (c.f. @LukePiette) resemble the early days of the online ads market 

If you were a big publisher (e.g. Conde Nast) you ran your own exchange and effectively supported credit to ad buyers who came direct to you. But then the remnant/secondary/non-publisher market grew and you found ad networks and demand side providers who aggregated remnant/secondary ad space selling people bundles that replicated the click through rate / false discovery rate of the primary publisher venues. 

Eventually, the market turned into a barbell/bimodal structure with FB/Google/TikTok being one end of purchasing spectrum and a number of other public ad networks taking the rest. Given the recent DoJ frontrunning cases against Amazon and Google, however,  combined with the much harder, collateralized credit needed for AI, you probably will have a different market structure for AI.

But there are definitely lessons from ads and crypto — especially in terms of who takes most of the value and who doesn’t (hint: how hard their technical solution was to implement doesn’t correspond with long term value capture)

text:
I’m a home builder. I walked the Salt Lake Temple grounds and came away amazed by a parking garage.

There’s a reflecting pool on the temple grounds. It sits on the roof of an underground parking garage. Cars below. Water above. Perfectly still.

Gets me every time.

We were in Utah to drop Jared off at BYU. Before we left, four generations of us walked through the new visitors’ center next to the temple. Tammy’s mom, Tammy and me, Jared and Grant, Elaine and her two children.

They give a guided tour of what happens inside a temple. There’s a scale model that opens up to show the rooms inside. Anyone can walk in and see it. I loved that. You get to see what these buildings mean to us.

There’s a large statue of Christ in there too. Really something to see.

The temple itself was built in the late 1800s. No modern equipment. No modern technology. Now they’re bringing it up to modern seismic standards.

I build homes for a living. I love remodeling. Creating. Taking something and making it better.

That’s exactly what they did here. The size of it. The age of it. I was in awe.

The temple opens to the public April 5 through October 1, 2027. Free tours. Tickets went live September 1. Link in the first comment.

We’ll be back.

Grateful for a trip with my family and a building that reminds me why I love what I do.

text:
The Casino Came First

Robinhood launched a chain on July 1 to put stocks onchain. Two months later it posted $4M in daily revenue, roughly 50x what Solana earned the same day, and a record $3.7B in 24-hour DEX volume. Very little of it came from stocks. It came from Pons, a memecoin launchpad that out-earned https://t.co/o23vEpQM3j, and from the 25,000 tokens it minted in a single day.

The easy read is that memes won again. The better read is what happened next. Traders started pairing those memes against tokenized stocks in the same pools, and the tokenized stocks, which had spent two years waiting for volume, suddenly had it. Over $3B of stock token volume, bootstrapped by assets that were never meant to be serious.

That reverses the story crypto has told itself. Serious assets were supposed to bring the liquidity. Instead they borrowed it.

Everyone drew the adoption path in the same direction: TradFi users arrive, tokenized stocks give them a reason to stay, liquidity follows. Robinhood ran it backwards. Speculation arrived first, liquidity pooled around it, and tokenized stocks were simply what that liquidity was sitting next to. If the order holds, tokenized stocks may not need TradFi users first. They may need crypto-native speculation first, and a venue that never separated the two. The wall between them was never about the assets. It was a product decision all along.

Yep, ESMT (3006) has exposure to multiple legacy memory segments.

Has a portfolio of: SLC/SPI NAND, NOR Flash, DDR2/DDR3, MCP/eMCP, so all the fun legacy stuff.

If you want to look at broader industry price hikes coming up that ESMT has exposure to:  

1. SLC NAND: ~120-170% for H2 2026.
2. DDR2: ~35-40% for Q3 2026.
3. DDR4: +30–40% Q3 (with DDR3 tightening)
4. NOR +60–65%+ for H2 (high density)
5. MCP/eMCP: maybe ~+15–25% QoQ for ESMT from my own estimate

For official breakdown:

DDR2 + DDR3: ~45% of revenue
DDR4/other DRAM ~ 10% of revenue
eMCP/MCP ≈30%
Analog + other ≈15%

Regardless, duration/hikes is the key: 

-> "none of the major global SLC NAND suppliers plan to add new production capacity in the near term."
-> TrendForce specifically expects depleted inventories to make SLC NAND even tighter in Q4.
-> Winbond withdrawing DDR2, would make inventory even tighter (and they're doing allocations into 2029-2030)
-> ESMT management said the market's main problem was supply, not demand; the company's foundry allocations covered only roughly 60–70% of customer orders
-> Nanya: "memory shortages could last through the end of 2027, with supply and demand still tight in 2028"
->Nanya explicitly said capacity constraints could cause shortages across DDR5, LPDDR5, DDR4, LPDDR4 and DDR3. 
-> ESMT included eMCP among the products receiving order-transfer benefits as mature node resources were being pulled elsewhere
______

If I had to state my thoughts again:

I think ESMT's ~1.9x July annualized run-rate P/E could compress further, despite factoring in PSMC's 45% wafer hike due to further legacy memory price hikes. 

Industry commentary supports durability throughout 2027. 

Cherry on top is if we start seeing LTAs and visibility into 2029-2030 (but not factored in). 

I think markets either don't know about this, are mispricing duration, or overestimating PSMC's wafer hike effects.

Nostalgia meta was the AI farm trial run and Chillhouse was the AI community trial run for Pumpfun. Once they had proof of concept, they expanded to Project Ascend and flooded X with 10x the number of inauthentic accounts/ botnets. Idk if you remember the Chillhouse launchpad with all the randomized AI Chillhouse memes? THAT was the same tool they used to make so many memes for the community.

text:
We are aware of a security incident on @Liquid_BTC. Purported white-hat hackers have withdrawn ~4,000 BTC (~$320 million) from the Liquid Federation wallet. The @Blockstream team is working on contacting them on-chain with a signed message.

What we know so far is that the funds were withdrawn via the SideSwap PAK (Peg-out Authorization Key), but that key was not compromised, nor were any others.

quoted_text:
“Nostalgia meta,”  

This is the period when onchain began to feel dangerous imo. 

It appears someone coordinated the launch of many coins. (Pumpfun imo)

The core tagline of “nostalgia” parroted by Alon and others was “we don’t need more coins, we need more success stories” 

Pumpfun took a coin called “COPE” and fabricated a narrative around it. The COPE dev spent a year deploying COPE coins and pushing the same meme. Pumpfun had him delete all mentions of the newer CAs so it appeared as if he had pushed the same coin for a year straight.  It was a great narrative. “Never give up” “support existing communities”etc. 

Then they bundled it and pumped it to 8 figures which created fomo around the meta and old deploys. 

They then released a story on their Instagram that Mitch had bought and sold for pennies and now he’s “coping” (ya ok lol)

I believe they used this meta as a way of directing Pumpfun users into chain wide farm prepared for almost a year. 

Hundreds if not thousands of coins were launched, then bundled slowly, quietly for nearly a year. 

It was impossible to tell they were bundled, because they had been accumulated over such a long period of time, in addition to being bought by wallets which were buying all of these coins. So it looked like regular degens. This is the same strategy Pumpfun uses for caballing their own coins - can’t tell which wallets are theirs because they own so many coins purchased over such a long period of time. 

All of these coins were invisible to terminals because they hadn’t migrated. There were no teams trying to get exposure. No calls. They weren’t mentioned or discovered by CT degens because no one was talking about them. And if they had been discovered? They likely would have automatically gone down. 

The charts appear totally normal / organic. The chart goes up and down for over a year, slowly rising in mc. 

But there’s ZERO mention of them anywhere across Twitter or telegram. None. “Nostalgia meta” starts and Cope is bundle pumped higher, hundreds of these Pumpfun bundle traps are also bundle pumped higher, graduate - and now are visible. At the same time Pumpfun’s people are dming KOLs the ca, Mitch and Pumpfun KOLs are buying. NOW you have noise. Now all of these coins are visible. 

Then if anyone actually buys them, the bundle start selling.

Maybe that person sells after a 70% retrace then the bundle pumps it back higher. Repeat. The ultimate rinsing. 

This is happening across hundreds maybe thousands of coins. Pumpfun users try to play the Pumpfun endorsed meta and just get rinsed over and over and over. 

I believe Pumpfun had their own messengers dming KOLs via TG- that way they buy and create visibility. I got the same dm many times, same words- different handles. 

“Mitch is in on side wallet” lmao ok.

I found that AB and some other core Pumpfun cabal people had a hand in a many coins at the same time. I was really impressed and confused because I couldn’t understand how that wasn’t idiotic. They really could trust a few people to have the inside scoop on so many coins at the same time? Well imo  it’s because those people likely were making their money in other ways, and far more of it. 

Towards the end of “nostalgia meta” after the entire space had been rinsed, AB tweets the below. Which even though it’s clearly a joke - imo combined with all the other circumstances feels a bit like an admission of guilt. This ofc is speculation. Not definitive proof, but enough for me to be convinced. 

I suspect these tactics are still being used by PF but in fresher coins and more fine tuned. IMO some of the same automated tech was used in “Mayham Mode”

Some of this is speculation but I wanted to share my thoughts because I’m nearly certain-  I know many have had similar observations and it’s time to start piecing this together

I am going to say something quite harsh here, and some of you won’t like it.

There are plenty of philosophers, posh James Orr types, who pontificate endlessly about democracy and why it is so brilliant and “sacred”. But in the real world, a world of injustice and competing human interests, democracy’s basic function is to mitigate violence and military-style takeovers.

Democracy exists, in large part, to dampen our violent instincts by creating a political process that is competitive, peaceful and broadly fair. You give people a mechanism for changing their government without having to overthrow it.

But there is a quid pro quo.

When democratic parties win power, they have to deliver on the promises they made to the electorate, particularly on something as existential as immigration. Otherwise, the entire point of the democratic process starts to unravel.

So ask yourself: what happens when parties repeatedly break their promises, ignore the electorate, gaslight people about what is happening around them, and even start imprisoning people for expressing political views?

Well, I’ll tell you.

The democratic contract is broken.

Foundant has launched Fia (Funder Intelligence Advisor), a new AI platform built specifically for social good organizations to address what the company calls the grantmaker's data dilemma: knowledge scattered across disconnected systems, insights that take days to compile, and manual reporting that pulls staff from mission-critical work.

Fia analyzes, indexes, and enriches data from a foundation's existing systems—including grants management, CRM, finance, SharePoint, and Google Drive—into one integrated knowledge base. Teams can access answers through natural conversation, automated reports, and custom workflows, with every response cited back to its underlying data.

The platform is currently in beta with early-adopter organizations. Foundant says Fia is designed to eventually operate independently of its other products, so organizations won't need to be current Foundant clients to access it once broadly available.

Foundant executives emphasized that AI use remains optional, clearly identified, and never used to train external models, with client data encrypted at every step. The company says Fia is part of a broader AI strategy that also includes AI features built into existing products and connectors for external tools like Claude and Copilot.
